reliancePower.name: Reliance Power
reliancePower.role: Runs the Sasan ultra mega coal plant and the Rosa plant, and is planning solar-plus-storage projects
strengths: Sasan is a low-cost plant with captive coal
Has cut debt in recent years
risks: Group legal and lender issues
Debt still high against its earnings

cesc.name: CESC
cesc.role: RP-Sanjiv Goenka group utility: Kolkata's licensed discom fed by its own Budge Budge and Haldia coal plants, plus distribution in Noida and franchises elsewhere
strengths: Regulated returns from an integrated Kolkata business
Expanding into renewables
risks: Regulatory dues and tariff orders
Coal costs

jpPower.name: Jaiprakash Power Ventures
jpPower.role: Runs the Vishnuprayag run-of-river hydro plant in Uttarakhand and the Bina and Nigrie coal plants in Madhya Pradesh
strengths: Hydro plant with low running costs
Nigrie has its own coal mine
risks: Uncertainty from the insolvency of its former parent, Jaiprakash Associates
Thermal tariffs depend on Madhya Pradesh

nava.name: Nava
nava.role: Runs the Maamba coal power plant in Zambia, plus ferro alloys and captive power in India
strengths: Maamba sells under a long-term power purchase agreement
Cash from collecting Zambian receivables
risks: Zambian currency and payment risk
Indian power is a small part of it

triveniTurbine.name: Triveni Turbine
triveniTurbine.role: Makes steam turbines for captive, waste-heat and biomass power plants, sold in India and abroad
strengths: A global leader in small steam turbines
Debt-free with a large aftermarket business
risks: Industrial capex cycles
Export competition from Chinese makers

tdPower.name: TD Power Systems
tdPower.role: Makes generators for steam, gas and hydro turbines, and traction motors
strengths: Supplies global turbine makers
Orders rising with gas and backup power demand
risks: Depends on a few large equipment-maker customers
Copper and steel costs

patelEng.name: Patel Engineering
patelEng.role: Civil contractor specialising in dams, tunnels and underground works for hydro projects
strengths: Long record in hydro tunnels and dams
Order book from NHPC and state hydro projects
risks: Stretched working capital
Geological surprises delay projects

hcc.name: Hindustan Construction Company
hcc.role: Builds hydro dams and tunnels, nuclear plants and transport infrastructure
strengths: Has built a large share of India's hydro capacity
Cut debt after selling assets
risks: Legacy debt and claims
Execution risk on large projects

kec.name: KEC International
kec.role: RPG group EPC major whose civil business builds residential, commercial and factory buildings, a small share next to power T&D
strengths: Civil arm builds housing, factories and data-centre buildings for private clients
Experienced EPC execution across segments
risks: Civil is a small slice of a power-led order book
Fixed-price contracts exposed to cement and steel costs

kpil.name: Kalpataru Projects International
kpil.role: EPC group whose buildings and factories business builds residential towers, offices and industrial projects; power T&D is its largest business
strengths: Large order book across several business lines
Execution record on towers and big complexes
risks: Buildings is a small segment next to power T&D
Fixed-price contracts expose it to steel and labour costs

aptus.name: Aptus Value Housing Finance
aptus.role: Home loans to self-employed families in South India, many in smaller towns where banks lend less
strengths: Focus on households that banks often skip
Strong in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh
risks: Southern concentration
Growth into new states is less proven

canFinHomes.name: Can Fin Homes
canFinHomes.role: Canara Bank-promoted home-loan company for salaried buyers, strongest in South India
strengths: Canara Bank parentage lowers its cost of funds
Salaried-borrower focus keeps credit quality steady
risks: Southern concentration
Thin spreads when rates move

piramalFinance.name: Piramal Finance
piramalFinance.role: Retail NBFC that lends for home purchase and affordable housing, with a shrinking legacy builder-loan book
strengths: Growing home-loan book built through its own branches
Years of experience financing developers
risks: Legacy real-estate wholesale loans still being run down
Retail growth must outpace the run-off

icicibank.name: ICICI Bank
icicibank.role: Second-largest private bank and one of the largest home-loan lenders, funding home buyers and builders
strengths: Large retail mortgage book across metros and smaller cities
Low-cost deposits fund long-tenor housing loans
risks: Housing loans are one part of a broad bank portfolio
Slower home sales or rate moves squeeze mortgage growth and spreads

vguard.name: V-Guard Industries
vguard.role: Sells house wires, cables, switchgear and MCBs, plus stabilisers, fans and water heaters, through electricians and dealers, strongest in South India
strengths: Wires and switchgear reach homes through electrician-led dealer networks
Strong brand in South Indian housing
risks: Copper costs squeeze wire margins
Larger wire makers compete for the same dealer shelf

sail.name: Steel Authority of India (SAIL)
sail.role: Largest state-owned steel maker; sells TMT rebar and structural sections for buildings alongside rails and plates
strengths: Government-owned scale and long supply history to big infrastructure and construction projects
Own iron-ore mines give it control of its main input
risks: Building steel is one slice of a commodity steel business, so earnings follow the steel cycle
Private makers and imports compete hard for rebar demand

pidilite.name: Pidilite Industries
pidilite.role: Maker of Fevicol carpentry adhesives and Dr Fixit waterproofing, sold through carpenters, plumbers and hardware shops into every new home
strengths: Fevicol and Dr Fixit are the default choice for carpenters and waterproofing contractors
Dealer and contractor reach follows every home that gets built or renovated
risks: Demand follows housing and renovation activity
Raw-material costs move margins

grasim.name: Grasim Industries
grasim.role: Aditya Birla group company whose Birla Opus is a large new decorative-paint brand sold to home owners and painters; also parent of UltraTech cement
strengths: Birla Opus built large paint capacity quickly and sells through a wide dealer network
Group ties to cement (UltraTech) put it across the housing build chain
risks: Paints are one segment of a holding company, so housing demand is diluted
Entering against entrenched paint leaders invites price competition

godrejProp.name: Godrej Properties
godrejProp.role: Pan-India residential developer, largely through joint-development and outright land deals in MMR, NCR, Pune, Bengaluru and Hyderabad
strengths: Largest Indian developer by booking value for three years running: record FY26 bookings of ₹34,171 Cr (+16%), beating guidance by 5%
Record FY26 operating cash flow (~₹7,830 Cr) and FY27 bookings guidance of ₹39,000 Cr
Godrej brand and a multi-city land pipeline added through JDAs and outright buys
risks: Reported profit lags bookings because revenue is recognised on completion; reported ROE is still single-digit
Aggressive land buying lifts net debt if sales slow
Stock has fallen in the year to Oct 2026 as the housing cycle cooled

dlf.name: DLF
dlf.role: Largest listed developer by market value: luxury housing in Gurugram plus a large office and mall rental business through DCCDL (a JV with GIC)
strengths: Net cash of ₹14,155 Cr at Mar 2026 with zero gross debt in the development business
FY26 bookings of ₹20,143 Cr; large low-cost Gurugram land bank supports high-margin luxury launches
Rental arm (DCCDL) adds steady office and mall income
risks: Bookings are lumpy: Q1 FY27 pre-sales were only ~₹657 Cr as launches were deferred
Heavy concentration in Gurugram luxury housing
FY27 guidance (₹20,000 Cr) depends on launches still pending

prestige.name: Prestige Estates Projects
prestige.role: Bengaluru-based developer of homes, offices, malls (Forum) and hotels, now expanding in MMR, NCR and Hyderabad
strengths: Record FY26 sales of ₹30,024 Cr, up 76% - the second-largest listed seller
Diversified rental base across office, retail and hospitality grows annuity income
Large launch pipeline across multiple cities
risks: Capital-heavy office, mall and hotel build-out raises debt
Execution risk as it scales in new cities outside Bengaluru
Profit has been volatile (FY25 net profit fell to ₹617 Cr)

lodha.name: Lodha Developers (Macrotech)
lodha.role: Largest MMR residential developer, also in Pune and Bengaluru, with a large land bank and industrial/data-centre park at Palava
strengths: FY26 pre-sales of ₹20,530 Cr (+16%) with record Q4 of ₹5,890 Cr
Added 12 projects worth ~₹60,000 Cr GDV in FY26 - 2.4x its original plan
Land bank at Palava supports housing, industrial parks and data centres for years
risks: Missed FY26 guidance of ₹21,000 Cr as March sales were deferred
Heavy MMR concentration
History of high leverage, now reduced; the new focus is free cash flow

oberoi.name: Oberoi Realty
oberoi.role: Mumbai developer of luxury homes, offices (Commerz), malls and hotels
strengths: Among the highest margins and ROCE in the listed sector
Growing rental income from Mumbai offices and malls (Oberoi Mall, Sky City)
Low debt and long-held, low-cost Mumbai land
risks: FY26 bookings rose only 4% to ₹5,447 Cr - growth depends on a few large launches
Entirely Mumbai-focused
Board approved raising up to ₹6,000 Cr, which could dilute shareholders

signature.name: Signatureglobal (India)
signature.role: Gurugram developer focused on mid-income and affordable group housing
strengths: Scaled fast in Gurugram's southern corridors (Sohna, Dwarka Expressway)
Collections of about ₹4,000 Cr in FY26
risks: FY26 pre-sales of ₹8,220 Cr fell well short of its ₹12,500 Cr guidance
Thin operating margins; FY26 profit was driven by one-off other income
Single-city exposure and higher sensitivity to home-loan rates

sobha.name: Sobha
sobha.role: Bengaluru-based developer that builds its own projects end to end (construction, interiors, glazing, concrete products)
strengths: Record FY26 bookings of ₹8,136 Cr (+30%); guides another ~30% growth in FY27
Backward integration gives quality control and a strong delivery reputation
Entered Mumbai luxury housing in FY26
risks: Low reported profit and ROE despite strong bookings
Bengaluru concentration
Integrated model ties up capital in manufacturing units

brigade.name: Brigade Enterprises
brigade.role: South India developer of homes, office parks (WTC), malls (Orion) and hotels
strengths: Balanced mix of residential sales and rental income
Strong brand in Bengaluru, Chennai and Hyderabad
Hotel arm listed separately (Brigade Hotel Ventures, 2025)
risks: Bengaluru is the bulk of sales and rental income
Rental assets add debt during build-out
Stock has fallen in the year to Oct 2026 as housing sentiment weakened

mahindraLifespace.name: Mahindra Lifespace Developers
mahindraLifespace.role: Mahindra group developer of homes and integrated industrial cities and clusters (Mahindra World City, Origins)
strengths: Industrial cluster land in Chennai and Jaipur sells to manufacturers and warehousing tenants
Mahindra brand and parent support
FY26 revenue more than tripled to ₹1,178 Cr as projects completed
risks: Still small; revenue and profit swing with project completions
Housing pre-sales scale is far below the leaders
Industrial land sales are lumpy

anantRaj.name: Anant Raj
anantRaj.role: Delhi-NCR land owner and developer of housing, and a builder of data-centre and IT-park capacity on its own land
strengths: Long-held, low-cost land bank in Delhi-NCR (Gurugram, Manesar, Delhi)
Revenue grew from ₹462 Cr (FY22) to ₹2,512 Cr (FY26) with low debt
Data-centre business on existing campuses adds a rental-style income stream
risks: Data-centre plans need heavy capex and anchor tenants
Concentrated in Delhi-NCR
Stock has been volatile after a large multi-year rally

embassyReit.name: Embassy Office Parks REIT
embassyReit.role: India's first listed REIT; Grade A office parks mainly in Bengaluru, plus Mumbai, Pune and Noida, and hotels
strengths: Q1 FY27 NOI up 17% to ₹1,020 Cr; occupancy 93% by value
GCCs took 81% of its Q1 FY27 leasing, at 11% re-leasing spreads
FY27 DPU guidance of ₹27.0-28.6 per unit
risks: Heavy Bengaluru exposure
Hotels add more volatile income
Rising bond yields can weigh on REIT unit prices

knowledgeReit.name: Knowledge Realty Trust
knowledgeReit.role: India's largest office REIT by gross asset value; Grade A offices in Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Gurugram and GIFT City
strengths: Sponsored by Blackstone and Sattva; about 46 msf of offices
~₹4,800 Cr IPO in Aug 2025 was subscribed ~12.5 times
Large Hyderabad and Bengaluru exposure to GCC demand
risks: Short listed track record and a part-year FY26
Hyderabad has more new office supply than other cities
Units have traded not far above the ₹100 issue price

mindspaceReit.name: Mindspace Business Parks REIT
mindspaceReit.role: K Raheja Corp-sponsored office REIT in Mumbai, Hyderabad, Pune and Chennai
strengths: Q1 FY27 NOI up 27.8% to ₹788 Cr; record DPU of ₹6.67 (+15%)
Committed occupancy 95.8% excluding recent acquisitions
Pipeline of sponsor assets to buy
risks: Hyderabad concentration and supply there
Growth relies partly on related-party acquisitions from the sponsor
Occupancy falls to ~92% including newly bought assets

brookfieldReit.name: Brookfield India Real Estate Trust
brookfieldReit.role: Brookfield-sponsored office REIT in Mumbai, Gurugram, Noida and Kolkata
strengths: Revenue more than tripled from FY22 to FY26 (₹877 Cr to ₹2,971 Cr) through acquisitions
Backed by one of the world's largest real-asset managers
risks: Some older SEZ parks and Kolkata/Noida assets lease more slowly
Acquisition-led growth adds debt and units
Reported profit is thin after interest and depreciation

bagmaneReit.name: Bagmane Prime Office REIT
bagmaneReit.role: Bengaluru-only office REIT (Bagmane tech parks), listed May 2026
strengths: Grade A parks in Bengaluru's main GCC corridors
Sixth listed REIT - adds depth to the market
risks: Single-city exposure
No meaningful listed financial history yet
Units have traded in a narrow range since listing

nexusReit.name: Nexus Select Trust
nexusReit.role: India's only listed retail REIT: Grade A malls in about 14 cities, sponsored by Blackstone
strengths: Pure play on Grade A mall consumption across many cities
Revenue-share leases let rent grow with tenant sales
Revenue grew from ₹1,916 Cr (FY24) to ₹2,568 Cr (FY26)
risks: Discretionary spending slowdown
Profit has fallen since listing due to tax and interest
Online and quick-commerce competition in some categories

phoenix.name: The Phoenix Mills
phoenix.role: India's largest listed mall owner-operator (Palladium, Phoenix Marketcity, Mall of Asia), plus offices and hotels
strengths: Q1 FY27 retail consumption up 32% to ₹4,727 Cr; FY26 up ~21%
Mall of Asia, Bengaluru nearly doubled consumption in Q1 FY27
Partnerships with GIC and CPP Investments fund expansion
risks: New malls take years to reach full rent
Valuation already prices in strong growth
Spending slowdown would hit revenue-share income

indospace.name: IndoSpace
indospace.role: India's largest Grade A industrial and logistics park platform
strengths: Largest pan-India network of logistics parks, backed by Everstone and global investors
risks: Unlisted - no public financials
notes: Privately held; backed by Everstone Group and global institutional capital
Leases warehouses to 3PL, e-commerce and manufacturing tenants

horizonParks.name: Horizon Industrial Parks (Blackstone)
horizonParks.role: Blackstone's Indian warehousing and industrial park platform - listed Aug 2026
strengths: Built on parks bought from Embassy Industrial Parks, with Blackstone capital for expansion
One of the few listed pure plays on Grade-A warehousing, a segment otherwise held by unlisted platforms
risks: Listed 24 Aug 2026 flat at its ₹60 issue price and has traded below it since - a weak start
Blackstone keeps control, and leasing depends on 3PL and e-commerce demand cycles
notes: Listed on NSE (HORIZONIND) and BSE on 24 Aug 2026 after a ₹2,600 Cr all-fresh-issue IPO

welspunOne.name: Welspun One
welspunOne.role: Warehousing developer and fund manager of the Welspun group
strengths: Fund-based model develops parks with institutional partners
risks: Unlisted - no public financials
notes: Develops Grade A warehousing through dedicated funds

infoEdge.name: Info Edge (India)
infoEdge.role: Owns 99acres, one of India's largest property portals; most revenue comes from Naukri (recruitment)
strengths: 99acres has strong brand recall among buyers and developers
Net-cash parent funds 99acres's growth
Large stakes in Eternal (Zomato) and PB Fintech
risks: Real estate is a small part of revenue and still in investment phase
Competition from Housing.com, MagicBricks and NoBroker
Reported profit swings with investee valuations

anarock.name: ANAROCK
anarock.role: Large residential brokerage, land and capital advisory, and research firm
strengths: Sells new launches for large developers across top cities; its research is widely quoted
risks: Unlisted - no public financials
notes: Privately held; founded by Anuj Puri
Publishes quarterly housing sales and supply data for the top 7 cities

noBroker.name: NoBroker
noBroker.role: Online rental and resale platform connecting owners and tenants directly, plus home services
strengths: Large user base in Bengaluru, Mumbai, Pune and Chennai rentals
risks: Unlisted - no public financials
notes: Earns from subscriptions, home loans and home services

squareYards.name: Square Yards
squareYards.role: Brokerage, property portal, mortgage and interiors platform
strengths: Combines brokerage with data, mortgages and interiors
risks: Unlisted - no public financials
notes: Privately held; operates in India and the Middle East

lt.name: Larsen & Toubro
lt.role: Builds high-rise towers, offices, airports, hospitals and factories through its Buildings & Factories business; also develops property through L&T Realty
strengths: Strongest balance sheet and execution record in Indian construction
Wins the largest and most complex building contracts
risks: Buildings is a small part of a much larger infrastructure, energy and defence group - not separately disclosed here

ahluwalia.name: Ahluwalia Contracts (India)
ahluwalia.role: Building contractor for hospitals, institutions, offices and residential towers
strengths: Pure play on building construction with a healthy ROCE
Revenue grew from ₹2,692 Cr (FY22) to ₹4,565 Cr (FY26)
risks: Profit fell in FY25 on cost overruns; margins remain volatile
Large share of government orders
Stock has fallen sharply in the year to Oct 2026

pspProjects.name: PSP Projects
pspProjects.role: Gujarat-based building contractor for institutional, industrial and residential projects
strengths: Revenue rose to ₹3,149 Cr in FY26
Adani Infra became a large shareholder in 2025, bringing a big potential client
risks: Profit collapsed from ₹167 Cr (FY22) to ₹56 Cr (FY26)
Gujarat concentration
Low ROE

capacite.name: Capacit'e Infraprojects
capacite.role: Contractor for high-rise residential and commercial towers, mainly in MMR, plus public housing
strengths: Specialist in tall buildings; trades at a low P/E
Profit grew from ₹48 Cr (FY22) to ₹193 Cr (FY26)
risks: Long receivable cycles with government housing clients
Small balance sheet
Stock has fallen sharply in the year to Oct 2026

ncc.name: NCC
ncc.role: Large contractor whose buildings segment (housing, hospitals, institutions) sits alongside water, roads and power work
strengths: Scale (~₹21,000 Cr revenue) and a large order book
Cheap valuation
risks: FY26 revenue fell ~6% as state-funded projects slowed
Heavy dependence on state government payments
Stock has fallen sharply in the year to Oct 2026

ultratech.name: UltraTech Cement
ultratech.role: India's largest cement maker (~200 MTPA); entering wires & cables
strengths: Q1 FY27 domestic volume up 13% with EBITDA of ₹1,214/t
Scale and national reach; target 242.5 MTPA by FY28
Acquisitions of India Cements and Kesoram add southern capacity
risks: Guided ₹130-140/t cost rise in Q2 FY27 from fuel and packaging
Prices rose only ~1% YoY in Q1 FY27
Wires & cables entry adds new execution risk

ambuja.name: Ambuja Cements
ambuja.role: Adani group cement maker, number two in India; absorbed Sanghi (effective 12 Mar 2026) and Penna (10 Apr 2026), and is merging in ACC (shareholders approved 29 Sep 2026, NCLT sanction pending) and Orient Cement
strengths: Fast capacity growth through acquisitions
Low-cost power and logistics through Adani group
risks: Integration of many acquired plants
Group-level governance scrutiny affects sentiment
Stock has fallen sharply in the year to Oct 2026

shreeCement.name: Shree Cement
shreeCement.role: Low-cost cement maker strong in north and east India
strengths: Among the lowest costs per tonne in the industry
Strong balance sheet
risks: Chose price over volume, losing share
FY25 profit halved; ROE is low
Expensive relative to earnings

dalmia.name: Dalmia Bharat
dalmia.role: Cement maker in east, north-east and south India
strengths: Low-carbon blended cement mix
FY26 profit rose ~65% to ₹1,157 Cr
risks: Weak pricing in the east and south
Low ROE
Expansion plans need large capex

jkCement.name: JK Cement
jkCement.role: Grey cement maker and India's second-largest white cement and wall-putty producer
strengths: White cement and putty sell into the finishing stage at higher margins
ROE among the best of the mid-size cement makers
risks: Expansion into new regions adds debt
Paints venture is still small

aplApollo.name: APL Apollo Tubes
aplApollo.role: India's largest structural steel tube maker - tubes for building frames, roofing, façades and warehouses
strengths: High ROCE and FY26 profit up ~59% to ₹1,203 Cr
Brand and dealer network let it charge more than commodity steel
Benefits as steel framing replaces concrete in some buildings
risks: Steel price swings affect volumes and inventory
Rich valuation

jswSteel.name: JSW Steel
jswSteel.role: India's largest private steel maker; TMT rebar (Neosteel) and coated sheets for building
strengths: Scale and integrated cost base
Safeguard duty on imports supports domestic prices
risks: Steel price cycles; construction is one of several end-uses
FY26 profit inflated by a one-off gain
High capex and debt

tataSteel.name: Tata Steel
tataSteel.role: Integrated steel maker; Tiscon rebar and roofing for homes and buildings
strengths: Tiscon is one of the strongest retail rebar brands
Low-cost Indian operations
risks: European operations have made losses
Steel price cycles

supreme.name: Supreme Industries
supreme.role: Largest plastics processor in India; plumbing pipes and fittings are most of its volume
strengths: Wide pipe and fittings range with a strong distribution network
Low debt and high ROCE
risks: PVC price falls cause inventory losses
Profit flat for four years (~₹950 Cr)

astral.name: Astral
astral.role: Branded CPVC/PVC pipes and fittings, adhesives (Resinova), bathware and paints
strengths: Strong brand in CPVC hot-water plumbing
Expanding into bathware and paints for the same dealers
risks: Profit flat at ~₹500-550 Cr since FY22
Rich valuation
PVC resin price swings

finolexInd.name: Finolex Industries
finolexInd.role: PVC pipes and fittings with its own PVC resin plant; agriculture-heavy
strengths: Own resin plant
Net cash
risks: Revenue has fallen four years in a row
Agriculture pipes dominate, so housing exposure is limited
Resin margins are volatile

princePipes.name: Prince Pipes and Fittings
princePipes.role: Plumbing and drainage pipes and fittings; Aquel bathware
strengths: Established brand in western and northern India
risks: Profit fell from ₹249 Cr (FY22) to ₹75 Cr (FY26)
Losing ground to larger rivals
Stock has fallen in the year to Oct 2026

polycab.name: Polycab India
polycab.role: India's largest wires and cables maker; house wires, switches, fans and lighting
strengths: Market leader in house wires with a large dealer and electrician network
Strong growth and ROCE
risks: New entrants (UltraTech, Adani) may raise competition
Copper price swings

havells.name: Havells India
havells.role: Switchgear, house wires, lighting, fans and appliances (Lloyd ACs)
strengths: Leading switchgear and wire brand with high ROCE
Strong retail network
risks: Lloyd ACs and consumer durables weigh on margins
Stock has fallen in the year to Oct 2026

kei.name: KEI Industries
kei.role: Power cables and house wires; growing retail wire share
strengths: Fast-growing retail house-wire business
New capacity at Sanand
risks: Institutional cables are a big share - housing exposure is partial
Copper price swings

finolexCables.name: Finolex Cables
finolexCables.role: House wires and cables with a strong retail brand in western and southern India
strengths: Trusted house-wire brand
Net cash
risks: Slower growth than larger rivals
Copper price swings

bluestar.name: Blue Star
bluestar.role: Central air-conditioning, MEP projects for offices, malls, hospitals and data centres, plus room ACs
strengths: Leader in commercial HVAC and MEP for Grade A offices
Growing room-AC share
risks: MEP contracts can carry cost overruns
A cool summer hurts room-AC sales

voltas.name: Voltas
voltas.role: Room-AC market leader (Tata group) with an MEP and HVAC projects business for buildings
strengths: Largest room-AC brand in India
Projects business for commercial buildings
risks: FY26 profit fell ~56% as AC demand weakened
Rising competition in room ACs

boschHomeComfort.name: Bosch Home Comfort India
boschHomeComfort.role: Hitachi-brand room ACs and VRF systems (formerly Johnson Controls-Hitachi Air Conditioning India)
strengths: Bosch ownership brings global HVAC technology and capital
risks: Loss-making or near break-even in most recent years
Small share against larger AC brands

kone.name: Kone Elevator India
kone.role: Elevators and escalators for residential towers, offices and malls
strengths: A market leader in Indian elevators with a large service base
risks: Unlisted Indian subsidiary of Finland's Kone - no Indian market data
notes: Lift maintenance contracts give recurring revenue

otis.name: Otis Elevator Company (India)
otis.role: Elevators and escalators, installation and maintenance
strengths: Global brand, large installed base in India
risks: Unlisted Indian subsidiary of US-listed Otis - no Indian market data

asianPaints.name: Asian Paints
asianPaints.role: India's largest paint maker; also home décor, kitchens and bath fittings
strengths: Largest dealer network and brand in decorative paints
High ROCE
risks: Birla Opus (Grasim) and other entrants have squeezed share and margins since 2024
Profit still below FY24 peak

bergerPaints.name: Berger Paints India
bergerPaints.role: Second-largest decorative paint maker; also industrial coatings
strengths: Strong in east and north India
High ROCE
risks: Same new-entrant pressure as the leader
FY26 profit slightly down

kajaria.name: Kajaria Ceramics
kajaria.role: India's largest ceramic and vitrified tile maker; also sanitaryware and faucets
strengths: Leading tile brand and dealer network; low debt
FY26 profit rose ~62% to ₹487 Cr
risks: Price competition from Morbi makers when exports weaken
Gas cost swings

cera.name: Cera Sanitaryware
cera.role: Sanitaryware, faucets and tiles for homes
strengths: Strong brand in mid-market bathrooms
Net cash
risks: FY26 profit fell ~17% to ₹204 Cr
Slow growth

centuryPly.name: Century Plyboards (India)
centuryPly.role: Plywood, laminates, MDF and particle board for interiors
strengths: Leading plywood brand
Revenue grew to ₹5,397 Cr in FY26
risks: New MDF plants cut returns while they ramp up
Timber cost swings

greenpanel.name: Greenpanel Industries
strengths: Scale in MDF
risks: Loss of ₹29 Cr in FY26 as MDF prices fell
Stock has fallen sharply in the year to Oct 2026

asahiGlass.name: Asahi India Glass
asahiGlass.role: Float and architectural glass for buildings; most revenue is car glass
strengths: Leading float and architectural glass maker
risks: Automotive glass is the larger business - building exposure is partial

hdfcBank.name: HDFC Bank
hdfcBank.role: Largest private-sector home lender since its 2023 merger with HDFC Ltd; also lends to developers
strengths: Large, low-cost deposit base
Mortgage book inherited from HDFC Ltd
risks: Home loans are one part of a broad banking book
Stock has fallen in the year to Oct 2026

sbi.name: State Bank of India
strengths: Lowest-cost funding and the widest branch reach
risks: Home loans are one part of a very large bank

lichf.name: LIC Housing Finance
lichf.role: Large housing finance company; mainly salaried home loans, plus developer loans
strengths: Low valuation; profit up ~2.5x since FY22
risks: Competition from banks on prime home loans
Developer loan book needs watching

bajajHfl.name: Bajaj Housing Finance
bajajHfl.role: Fast-growing HFC: home loans, lease-rental discounting and developer finance
strengths: Bajaj Finance parentage and strong credit ratings
Profit up ~18% in FY26 to ₹2,560 Cr
risks: Developer and lease-rental loans add risk
Trades at a premium to other housing lenders, and the stock has fallen in the year to Oct 2026

pnbHousing.name: PNB Housing Finance
pnbHousing.role: HFC lending to salaried and self-employed homebuyers, pushing into affordable housing
strengths: Profit up ~2.7x since FY22 after a turnaround
Stock has risen strongly in the year to Oct 2026
risks: Management change after the CEO's 2025 exit
Affordable expansion raises credit risk

aadharHfc.name: Aadhar Housing Finance
aadharHfc.role: Affordable housing lender to low- and middle-income borrowers (Blackstone-backed)
strengths: Large affordable lender with a healthy ROE
Profit up ~20% in FY26
risks: Informal-income borrowers are more sensitive to rate hikes

aavas.name: Aavas Financiers
aavas.role: Affordable housing lender focused on rural and semi-urban Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra
strengths: Steady profit growth; low credit losses
risks: State concentration
Stock has fallen in the year to Oct 2026

homeFirst.name: Home First Finance Company India
homeFirst.role: Affordable housing lender to salaried borrowers in urban areas
strengths: Profit up ~41% in FY26 to ₹540 Cr
Technology-led underwriting
risks: Faster growth may raise future credit losses

acc.name: ACC
acc.role: Adani group cement maker selling bagged cement through dealers and ready-mix concrete to building sites across India; shareholders have approved its merger into Ambuja Cements
strengths: Plants spread across India and one of the oldest cement brands
Ready-mix concrete arm sells straight to developers and contractors
risks: The pending merger into Ambuja Cements will end it as a separate listed company
Cement prices and fuel costs swing its margins

ramcoCement.name: Ramco Cements
ramcoCement.role: South India's leading cement maker, also selling dry-mix mortar, ready-mix and construction chemicals to builders
strengths: Strong brand and dealer network across Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
Own limestone and captive power keep costs low
risks: Southern cement prices are among the most volatile in India
Debt from its capacity build-out, which it is cutting by selling surplus land

jswCement.name: JSW Cement
jswCement.role: JSW group cement maker built around slag cement from JSW Steel's blast furnaces, with plants in the South, West and East; listed Aug 2025
strengths: Cheap slag from group steel plants gives it a cost and low-carbon edge
Group backing for a large capacity expansion
risks: A younger and smaller brand than the market leaders
Expansion spending ahead of demand in its regions

nuvoco.name: Nuvoco Vistas
nuvoco.role: Nirma group cement maker (Concreto, Duraguard), a leader in East India, with a large ready-mix concrete business; bought Vadraj Cement in 2025
strengths: Leading brands in East India, the fastest-growing cement region
Ready-mix and building-materials arm sells straight to sites
risks: Debt from acquisitions, including Vadraj Cement
Price competition in the East as rivals add capacity

indiaCements.name: India Cements
indiaCements.role: Southern cement maker controlled by UltraTech since Dec 2024, whose plants are being upgraded and run within UltraTech's network
strengths: UltraTech's ownership brings cost, fuel and distribution support
Limestone reserves and plants across the South
risks: Has posted losses while its older plants are upgraded
Minority shareholders depend on how UltraTech integrates it

abrel.name: Aditya Birla Real Estate
abrel.role: Formerly Century Textiles: through Birla Estates it develops premium homes in Mumbai (Worli), NCR, Pune and Bengaluru, after selling its pulp and paper business to ITC
strengths: Aditya Birla group brand and owned land, including Worli in Mumbai
Growing launch pipeline through joint-development deals
risks: Has reported losses while its projects are being built
Profit is booked only on handover, so results lag bookings

sunteck.name: Sunteck Realty
sunteck.role: Mumbai developer of luxury and mid-income homes in BKC, Oshiwara, Naigaon and Vasind, plus a few commercial projects
strengths: Low-debt balance sheet
Asset-light joint-development deals across the Mumbai region
risks: Concentrated in the Mumbai region
Revenue is lumpy because it is booked on project completion

puravankara.name: Puravankara
puravankara.role: Bengaluru developer selling homes under the Purva and Provident brands in Bengaluru, Pune, Mumbai and Chennai
strengths: Long record in Bengaluru, one of India's strongest housing markets
Land bank across southern and western cities
risks: Higher debt than most listed developers
Profit recognition lags bookings, so results swing

raymondRealty.name: Raymond Realty
raymondRealty.role: Real estate arm demerged from Raymond in 2025: builds homes on Raymond's own land in Thane and runs joint-development projects in Mumbai
strengths: Large owned land parcel in Thane at low land cost
Adding asset-light joint-development projects in Mumbai suburbs
risks: Most of its pipeline sits in one Thane location
A short record as a separate listed company

nbcc.name: NBCC (India)
nbcc.role: PSU project manager and builder that redevelops government colonies in Delhi (East Kidwai Nagar, Sarojini Nagar) and sells the commercial and housing space it builds
strengths: Large order book from central ministries, PSUs and state governments
Asset-light project-management model with little debt
risks: Depends on government orders and approvals to sell redeveloped land
Slow sales of redevelopment space hold back cash

jindalSteel.name: Jindal Steel
jindalSteel.role: Integrated steelmaker (formerly Jindal Steel & Power) selling TMT rebar, structural sections and plates from Angul and Raigarh to construction
strengths: One of India's largest makers of rebar and heavy structurals
The Angul expansion adds flat steel and lowers costs
risks: Steel price cycles and cheap imports
Coking-coal costs and a heavy expansion bill

shyamMetalics.name: Shyam Metalics
shyamMetalics.role: Eastern India maker of pellets, sponge iron, ferro alloys and TMT and structural steel, also adding aluminium foil and battery materials
strengths: Integrated low-cost plants with captive power
Spread across steel, alloys and new materials
risks: Construction steel is only part of its sales
Steel and ferro-alloy price cycles

gallantt.name: Gallantt Ispat
gallantt.role: Steel maker in Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat selling Gallantt TMT bars, backed by its own sponge iron and power plants
strengths: Integrated from sponge iron to TMT with captive power
Strong regional rebar brand in Uttar Pradesh
risks: A small regional player beside the integrated majors
Steel price cycles

vedantaIronSteel.name: Vedanta Iron and Steel
vedantaIronSteel.role: Iron and steel business demerged from Vedanta in 2026: ESL Steel at Bokaro makes TMT bars, wire rods and pig iron, beside iron-ore mines
strengths: Iron ore from group mines feeds the steel plant
Bokaro plant sells long products into eastern India
risks: A short record as a separate listed company
Steel price cycles and iron-ore costs

rrKabel.name: RR Kabel
rrKabel.role: House-wire and cable maker (RR Kabel) that also sells fans, lights and switches
strengths: Strong retail house-wire brand with electrician loyalty programmes
Growing cables and export business
risks: Copper price swings
Competition from Polycab, Havells and new entrants such as UltraTech

kansaiNerolac.name: Kansai Nerolac
kansaiNerolac.role: Decorative and industrial paint maker controlled by Japan's Kansai Paint; the leader in automotive coatings
strengths: Market leader in automotive and industrial coatings
Long-established decorative brand and dealer reach
risks: Price war in decorative paints since Birla Opus entered
Crude-linked raw-material costs

jswDulux.name: JSW Dulux
jswDulux.role: Dulux decorative paint maker, formerly Akzo Nobel India, bought by JSW Paints in 2025 and renamed
strengths: Dulux is one of India's best-known premium paint brands
JSW group scale and distribution behind it
risks: Merging with JSW Paints while the decorative price war runs
Lost its powder coatings arm to AkzoNobel in the sale

indigoPaints.name: Indigo Paints
indigoPaints.role: Decorative paint maker that built its brand on niche products (metallic emulsions, floor coats) and small-town dealers
strengths: Distinctive products and strong reach in smaller towns
Little debt
risks: Small scale against Asian Paints, Birla Opus and JSW
Margin pressure from price cuts

greenply.name: Greenply Industries
greenply.role: Plywood and decorative veneer maker that has added MDF boards
strengths: Leading national plywood brand
MDF plant widens its range beyond plywood
risks: Timber cost swings
Competition from unorganised plywood makers

honeywellAuto.name: Honeywell Automation India
honeywellAuto.role: Supplies building management, fire alarm and security systems for offices, airports and hospitals, beside its larger industrial automation business
strengths: Honeywell's global technology and brand
Debt-free with large cash reserves
risks: Buildings are one segment beside industrial automation
The parent's break-up into separate companies may reshape its product lines

piind.name: PI Industries
piind.role: Agrochemical custom-synthesis leader whose pharma arm (PI Health Sciences) offers contract development and manufacturing to drug companies
strengths: Process chemistry and long-contract habits carried over from agrochemicals
Plants and teams added to build a pharma arm
risks: Pharma is a small, newer arm next to agrochemicals
Winning trust with pharma innovators takes years

jubilantIngrevia.name: Jubilant Ingrevia
jubilantIngrevia.role: Pyridine and picoline maker whose intermediates and vitamin B3 are sold to API and drug makers
strengths: One of the largest pyridine makers in the world
Integrated chemistry from basic feedstocks
risks: Pharma is only part of a business that also sells acetyls and other chemicals
China competition in pyridines

navinfluor.name: Navin Fluorine International
navinfluor.role: Fluorine specialist whose contract-manufacturing arm makes fluorinated intermediates and APIs for pharma innovators
strengths: Fluorine chemistry know-how that few Indian CDMOs match
Multi-year contracts with innovator companies
risks: CDMO is a smaller part next to refrigerants and specialty chemicals
Innovator drug-launch timing sets demand

acutaas.name: Acutaas Chemicals
acutaas.role: Gujarat specialty chemicals maker whose main business is pharma intermediates and APIs for regulated-market drug makers, plus CDMO work
strengths: Pharma intermediates are most of its sales
Contract work with innovator companies keeps orders repeating
risks: Concentrated in a few products and customers
Customer qualification cycles delay new orders

sunPharma.name: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries
sunPharma.role: India's largest drugmaker: No. 1 in the Indian branded market, a growing global innovative-medicines (specialty) business and US generics via Sun and Taro
strengths: Global innovative medicines (Ilumya, Cequa, Winlevi, Leqselvi, Unloxcyt) were ~22% of sales in Q1 FY27 and growing double digits - the largest specialty franchise of any Indian company
No. 1 by share in the Indian pharmaceutical market with a chronic-heavy portfolio
Agreed (Apr 2026) to buy Organon for US$11.75bn EV - adds women's health, biosimilars and ~140-country reach; combined revenue ~US$12.4bn per company
risks: Organon deal (expected to close early 2027) takes net debt/EBITDA to ~2.3x and brings integration risk
US generics fell ~10% YoY in Q1 FY27 on price erosion; Halol remains OAI (Jun 2025) and under import alert
Specialty launch spending (Leqselvi, Unloxcyt) is now a structural cost

mankind.name: Mankind Pharma
mankind.role: India-focused branded generics leader - No. 1 by prescription volume, strong in tier-2/3 towns, plus OTC brands and (since 2024) Bharat Serums & Vaccines
strengths: Almost all revenue is domestic, so no US price-erosion or tariff exposure
Deep rural/semi-urban distribution and top-10 brands (Manforce, Prega News, Moxikind) built at low marketing cost
Bharat Serums & Vaccines acquisition adds women's health, critical care and biologics capability
risks: Bharat Serums deal (~₹13,600 Cr EV) was debt-funded - FY26 profit slipped on interest and amortisation despite 17% revenue growth
Acute and mass-market mix is more exposed to NLEM price caps and trade-generic competition
Integration execution on a large acquisition is new for the company

torrent.name: Torrent Pharmaceuticals
torrent.role: Chronic-focused branded formulations (cardiac, CNS, GI, diabetes) in India, Brazil and Germany; absorbed J B Chemicals in 2026
strengths: Among the most productive Indian field forces, with ~55%+ of revenue from India branded formulations
J B Chemicals (Cilacar, Rantac, Metrogyl and ex-Sanofi/Novartis brands) consolidated from Jan 2026 and amalgamated in Jul 2026 - India revenue rose 43% YoY in Q4 FY26
Track record of buying and re-energising brands (Elder, Unichem India, Curatio)
risks: Rich valuation leaves little room for integration slips
Acquisition and exceptional charges cut Q4 FY26 profit 27% YoY
Small US business with past USFDA issues at Indrad and Dahej

alkem.name: Alkem Laboratories
alkem.role: Top-5 Indian branded formulations company, strongest in anti-infectives and GI (Clavam, Pan), with a US generics arm and Enzene biologics/CDMO subsidiary
strengths: Leader in acute therapies with very wide doctor and chemist reach
US generics (~20% of sales) adds diversification with modest concentration
Enzene subsidiary gives an option on biosimilars and biologics CDMO
risks: Acute/anti-infective mix grows slower than chronic and faces NLEM price control
Enzene still loss-making and needs capital
Income-tax provisions have hit profit before (FY23) and disputes remain an overhang

abbottIndia.name: Abbott India
abbottIndia.role: Indian listed arm of Abbott Laboratories selling branded formulations (Thyronorm, Duphaston, Udiliv, Digene) - a pure domestic play
strengths: Very high returns on capital with no debt and a healthy dividend yield
100% domestic - insulated from US pricing, tariffs and USFDA risk
Strong women's health, thyroid and GI brands with parent's global pipeline to in-license
risks: Slow growth for a premium valuation - revenue CAGR ~9% FY22-FY26
Relies heavily on contract manufacturers and on the parent for new products
Exposure to NLEM price caps on several key brands

cipla.name: Cipla
cipla.role: No. 3 Indian branded formulations company and respiratory specialist, with a US complex-generics (inhalers, peptides) business and South Africa
strengths: India's respiratory/inhalation leader - India is the largest and fastest-growing segment ('One India' had a record Q1 FY27)
US inhaler capability: gAdvair Diskus approved Jul 2026 from its New York plant (US onshore - a tariff hedge), gAlbuterol, gVentolin
Net-cash balance sheet
risks: gRevlimid has ended and lanreotide supply was disrupted - Q1 FY27 profit fell 39% YoY
North America revenue (~US$160m a quarter) depends on a few complex launches arriving on time
USFDA compliance history at Goa and other sites

eris.name: Eris Lifesciences
eris.role: Chronic-focused Indian branded formulations (diabetes, cardiac, derma) built through acquisitions, now including insulins and injectables
strengths: Almost entirely domestic and chronic-weighted portfolio with high gross margins
Bought Biocon's Indian branded formulations and insulin brands and Swiss Parenterals - moves it into injectables and insulins
FY26 profit jumped to ₹648 Cr as acquisitions matured
risks: Acquisition-led growth has raised leverage and amortisation
Insulin and injectables are new manufacturing capabilities
Semaglutide and SGLT2 generics intensify competition in its core diabetes franchise

ipca.name: Ipca Laboratories
ipca.role: Vertically integrated maker of branded formulations (pain - Zerodol, anti-malarials, cardiac) and APIs, with Unichem adding US/Europe generics
strengths: Backward integration into its own APIs protects margins in pain and anti-malarial franchises
India branded growth consistently above market in pain/rheumatology
Unichem acquisition (2023) gives a ready US and European generics platform
risks: Past USFDA import alert (2015) on key sites still shapes US ambitions
Anti-malarial institutional business is tender-driven and lumpy
Unichem integration and margin repair are still in progress

zydus.name: Zydus Lifesciences
zydus.role: Diversified major: US generics (~45% of sales), India branded formulations, consumer wellness, vaccines/biosimilars and an in-house NCE pipeline
strengths: Rare Indian NCE track record - saroglitazar (Lipaglyn) and desidustat discovered in-house
Strong US limited-competition products (gMyrbetriq/mirabegron, transdermals, injectables)
Consumer wellness (Complan, Glucon-D, Nycil) and launched generic semaglutide in India (Mar 2026)
risks: US earnings concentration in a few products, including mirabegron with patent-litigation risk
US generic tariff clock from Aug 2028 without US manufacturing
NCE development spend with binary outcomes (saroglitazar PBC trials)

ajanta.name: Ajanta Pharma
ajanta.role: Branded generics in India (cardiac, ophthalmology, derma), Asia and Africa, plus a US generics business
strengths: ~70% of revenue from branded markets (India, Asia, Africa) - less exposed to US price erosion
High returns on capital and consistent dividend/buyback payouts
India growth above market in chronic niches
risks: Africa institutional anti-malarial business is tender-driven
US is a smaller, price-eroding generics book
Currency risk in African and Asian markets

intas.name: Intas Pharmaceuticals
intas.role: Unlisted top-3 Indian drugmaker - India branded formulations plus Accord (Europe/US generics) and Accord BioPharma biosimilars
strengths: Among the largest Indian companies by revenue, with leading European generics and oncology/biosimilar businesses
risks: Unlisted - no public market data; past USFDA observations at its Ahmedabad plants
notes: One of India's top-3 companies in the domestic market and a large exporter via Accord Healthcare
No listed market data - figures not available

glenmark.name: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals
glenmark.role: Branded formulations (India derma/respiratory, Europe, emerging markets), US generics and the Ichnos Glenmark Innovation (IGI) biotech arm
strengths: IGI licensed trispecific antibody ISB 2001 to AbbVie for US$700m upfront plus up to US$1.225bn milestones and royalties (Sep 2025) - the biggest Indian out-licensing deal
Ryaltris (nasal spray) is a growing global specialty brand
Debt reduced after selling Glenmark Life Sciences (API) to Nirma
risks: FY26 profit is inflated by the one-off AbbVie upfront - FY27 comparisons will be tough
Repeated USFDA compliance setbacks at several plants have held back US launches
Innovation spend remains high relative to the base business

lupin.name: Lupin
lupin.role: US complex generics (inhalation, injectables), India branded formulations and specialty assets
strengths: Turnaround complete: FY26 net profit ₹5,355 Cr vs a FY22 loss, with high ROCE
Leading US respiratory generics (gSpiriva, albuterol) and limited-competition launches (tolvaptan, mirabegron)
Growing India chronic business and European specialty (VISUfarma ophthalmics)
risks: US profit concentration in a few products that will see more competitors
US generic tariff schedule from Aug 2028 for India-made product
USFDA status at Pithampur, Mandideep and other sites

wockhardt.name: Wockhardt
wockhardt.role: Antibiotic discovery company - first Indian-discovered NCE antibiotic approved by the US FDA (Zaynich, 2026) - plus generics in India, UK and emerging markets
strengths: Zaynich (cefepime-zidebactam) approved by USFDA (mid-2026) for drug-resistant infections; EMA filing accepted for accelerated assessment
Novel antibiotic pipeline (Miqnaf/nafithromycin approved in India)
FY26 was the first profitable year after a long loss run
risks: Commercial success of a new antibiotic in the US is notoriously hard (hospital uptake, stewardship)
History of USFDA import alerts and leverage
Valuation now prices in a successful Zaynich launch

sparc.name: SPARC (Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company)
sparc.role: Sun Pharma group's pure R&D company developing novel drugs and delivery platforms for out-licensing
strengths: Pure-play exposure to Indian drug discovery with Sun Pharma backing
Won a US FDA priority review voucher with Sezaby (Feb 2026) and sold it for US$195m
risks: No recurring revenue - FY26 profit is the one-off voucher; the business is otherwise loss-making
Binary clinical outcomes and past pipeline setbacks
Depends on licensing partners and funding

medplus.name: MedPlus Health Services
medplus.role: India's second-largest pharmacy retail chain, with a large private-label generics push
strengths: Thousands of stores concentrated in south India with improving store maturity
Private-label generics lift gross margins well above branded resale
Profit rising steadily from a thin base (FY26 ₹220 Cr)
risks: Thin margins - pharmacy EBITDA in mid-single digits
Diagnostics expansion has diluted returns
Regulatory risk on trade margins and online pharmacy rules

apolloHosp.name: Apollo Hospitals Enterprise
apolloHosp.role: Hospital group whose Apollo HealthCo arm runs India's largest pharmacy chain (7,000+ stores), Apollo 24/7 and, via Keimed, wholesale pharma distribution
strengths: Largest organised pharmacy network and wholesale arm (Keimed) give real scale in drug distribution
Pharmacy and digital business is being demerged into Apollo Healthtech for a separate listing (targeted Q4 FY27)
risks: Pharmacy is a minority of value inside a hospital-led group until the demerger completes
Apollo 24/7 digital losses and demerger execution risk

entero.name: Entero Healthcare Solutions
entero.role: Pan-India pharma and healthcare-product distributor consolidating fragmented regional wholesalers
strengths: Fast growth from acquisitions and new territories - revenue up ~2.6x FY22-FY26
Turned profitable and scaling margins as acquired distributors integrate
risks: Thin distribution margins and high working capital
Acquisition-integration risk; ROE still single digit

pharmEasy.name: PharmEasy (API Holdings)
pharmEasy.role: Unlisted e-pharmacy and B2B distribution platform (PharmEasy, Retailio, Thyrocare parent)
strengths: One of the largest digital pharmacy and pharma B2B platforms in India
risks: Unlisted; heavy losses and a steep down-round rights issue led by Manipal group in 2023
notes: Withdrew its IPO in 2022; recapitalised in 2023

tata1mg.name: Tata 1mg
tata1mg.role: Unlisted e-pharmacy, diagnostics and teleconsultation platform owned by Tata Digital
strengths: Backed by the Tata group's balance sheet and Tata Neu ecosystem
risks: Unlisted; loss-making and part of a larger digital-consumer portfolio

drReddy.name: Dr Reddy's Laboratories
drReddy.role: US generics major (largest single market), India branded formulations, emerging markets, APIs (PSAI) and biosimilars
strengths: Net-cash balance sheet and diversified geographies (US, India, Russia/CIS, Europe)
Among the first with generic semaglutide in India (Obeda, Mar 2026), with other semaglutide markets to follow
Consumer health platform (Nicotinell bought from Haleon) and biosimilars pipeline
risks: gRevlimid's end cut US sales and Q1 FY27 profit sharply; a semaglutide API provision (~₹240 Cr per reports) added to the hit
US generic tariff clock from Aug 2028
Higher solvent and freight costs (Middle East conflict) pressured margins

aurobindo.name: Aurobindo Pharma
aurobindo.role: Largest Indian exporter of generics to the US by volume, with Eugia injectables, Europe, APIs and a Pen-G KSM project
strengths: Huge US portfolio and among the deepest ANDA pipelines - low dependence on any single product
Backward integrated from KSMs (Pen-G/6-APA plant under PLI) to APIs to formulations
CuraTeQ biosimilars and European business diversify earnings
risks: Eugia sterile sites under USFDA action: Unit III WL (2024), Unit II OAI (Mar 2026), Unit I WL (Aug 2026, ~2% of revenue)
High US exposure (~45% of sales) to price erosion and the 2028 tariff clock
Low ROE versus peers

alembic.name: Alembic Pharmaceuticals
alembic.role: US generics (oral solids, injectables, oncology, derma) with India branded formulations and APIs
strengths: Large US approval count with new injectable/oncology capacity now built
India branded and API businesses add stability
Big capex cycle largely complete - operating leverage ahead if utilisation rises
risks: New plants carry depreciation before they fill, holding ROCE down
US price erosion in oral solids
Stock derated in the five years to Oct 2026

natco.name: Natco Pharma
natco.role: Niche US generics through Para IV challenges and partners (gRevlimid with Teva), India oncology, agrochemicals and an Africa platform
strengths: Proven Para IV/first-to-file skill - gRevlimid earned outsized profits FY24-FY25
Net-cash balance sheet; now 49% of South Africa's Adcock Ingram (Jul 2026)
First wave of generic semaglutide in India at ~₹1,290 a month
risks: gRevlimid volume-limited deal ended Jan 2026 - FY26 profit fell 25% and FY27 resets lower
Lumpy earnings tied to a few launches and litigation outcomes
Agrochemical and Africa diversification are unproven at scale

granules.name: Granules India
granules.role: Vertically integrated maker of high-volume molecules (paracetamol, metformin, ibuprofen) from KSM to API to formulations, mainly for the US
strengths: Cost leadership in a few large-volume molecules with integration from PAP (KSM) through finished dosage
Building a US formulation base and peptide CDMO (Senn Chemicals, Switzerland)
FY26 profit +19% with improving mix
risks: Gagillapur warning letter (Feb 2025) blocks new approvals from that site (nine products awaiting)
Molecule concentration exposes it to Chinese price cuts
US generic tariff clock

senores.name: Senores Pharmaceuticals
senores.role: Young US-focused generics company with an Atlanta (US) manufacturing site plus emerging-market and critical-care injectables
strengths: US-based plant (Atlanta) qualifies for US government contracts and is a natural tariff hedge
Fast growth from a small base (FY26 revenue ₹633 Cr, PAT ₹122 Cr)
risks: Small scale and short listed history (Dec 2024)
Depends on partner-led US launches and acquisitions

sigachi.name: Sigachi Industries
sigachi.role: One of the world's largest makers of microcrystalline cellulose (MCC), a key tablet excipient
strengths: Global MCC supplier qualified with large generic makers; capacity being added at Dahej and Jhagadia
risks: June 2025 explosion at its Pashamylaram (Telangana) plant killed over 40 workers - FY26 swung to a loss and safety/legal liabilities remain
Small company with concentrated product line

borosilSci.name: Borosil Scientific
borosilSci.role: Laboratory glassware and instruments plus pharma primary packaging (Klasspack vials, ampoules and cartridges)
strengths: Direct exposure to injectable and lab demand via Klasspack primary packaging
Brand leadership in Indian lab glassware
risks: Very small company, and the stock has fallen in the year to Oct 2026
Competes with SCHOTT Poonawalla and imports in pharma glass

schottPoonawalla.name: SCHOTT Poonawalla
schottPoonawalla.role: Unlisted maker of Type-I borosilicate glass vials, ampoules, cartridges and prefilled syringes for injectables
strengths: India's leading pharma primary-packaging maker, owned with Germany's SCHOTT group
risks: Unlisted - no public market data
notes: Joint venture of SCHOTT AG with the Poonawalla family
Supplies vaccine and injectable makers globally

acg.name: ACG Worldwide
acg.role: Unlisted maker of empty hard capsules, barrier films/foils and pharma processing and packaging machinery
strengths: Among the world's largest empty-capsule makers, integrated with packaging films and equipment
risks: Unlisted - no public market data
notes: Mumbai-based, family-owned with private-equity minority investors

gland.name: Gland Pharma
gland.role: B2B sterile injectables developer and contract manufacturer (vials, bags, prefilled syringes) for global generic and innovator companies; owns Cenexi in Europe
strengths: Pure-play injectables with a long USFDA-compliant record in Hyderabad
Recovery under way: FY26 profit ₹1,027 Cr (+47%); stock recovered strongly from its 52-week low in the year to Oct 2026
Building GLP-1 / peptide fill-finish and biologics CDMO capacity
risks: Controlled by China's Shanghai Fosun Pharma - a perception risk with US customers in a BIOSECURE world
Cenexi (France) turnaround still dilutes margins
Customer and product concentration

caplin.name: Caplin Point Laboratories
caplin.role: Branded generics in Latin America plus Caplin Steriles, a growing US injectables and ophthalmics business
strengths: Net-cash, high-return and steady growth - FY26 profit ₹650 Cr
US sterile pipeline building from Chennai plants with clean regulatory record
risks: Latin America currency and political risk
US injectables pricing as more Indian capacity comes on

piramalPharma.name: Piramal Pharma
piramalPharma.role: Global CDMO (Piramal Pharma Solutions), complex hospital generics (inhaled anaesthetics, intrathecal therapies) and India consumer health
strengths: Integrated CDMO network in India, UK and North America with ADC and high-potency capability
Piramal Critical Care is a top inhaled-anaesthetics supplier worldwide
risks: FY26 net loss of ₹326 Cr as CDMO customers destocked
Leverage and very low ROCE
Customer-specific inventory cycles make earnings lumpy

biocon.name: Biocon
biocon.role: India's largest biosimilars company (Biocon Biologics, now 100% owned) plus generics/APIs and a majority stake in Syngene
strengths: Broad commercial biosimilar portfolio (insulins, trastuzumab, bevacizumab, adalimumab, aflibercept, ustekinumab, denosumab)
Full ownership of Biocon Biologics completed in 2026 (Viatris, Serum and minority stakes swapped in)
Majority shareholder of Syngene (CRO/CDMO)
risks: High leverage from the Viatris biosimilars deal - FY26 profit just ₹369 Cr, ROE near zero
Biosimilar price erosion as more competitors launch
Past USFDA issues at Bengaluru and Malaysia sites

serum.name: Serum Institute of India
serum.role: Unlisted - world's largest vaccine maker by doses (measles, DTP, pneumococcal, HPV, malaria R21)
strengths: Unmatched scale and WHO-prequalified portfolio supplying Gavi/UNICEF
risks: Unlisted - no public market data
notes: Owned by the Poonawalla family (Cyrus Poonawalla group)

bharatBiotech.name: Bharat Biotech
bharatBiotech.role: Unlisted vaccine developer (Covaxin, Rotavac, typhoid conjugate, nasal COVID vaccine)
strengths: Own R&D-led vaccine portfolio with WHO prequalifications
risks: Unlisted - no public market data; post-COVID revenue normalisation

biologicalE.name: Biological E
biologicalE.role: Unlisted vaccine and biologics maker (Corbevax, PCV14, pentavalent, typhoid)
strengths: Large-scale WHO-prequalified vaccine supplier and contract manufacturer for global partners
risks: Unlisted - no public market data

panacea.name: Panacea Biotec
panacea.role: Listed vaccine maker - WHO-prequalified pentavalent (Easyfive-TT) for UNICEF/Gavi, and a dengue vaccine (DengiAll) in Phase 3 with ICMR
strengths: One of the few listed pure-play vaccine makers in India
Dengue vaccine is a large optionality if Phase 3 succeeds
risks: Loss-making since FY23; FY22 profit was a one-off brand sale to Mankind
Tender-driven revenue and binary clinical outcome

divis.name: Divi's Laboratories
divis.role: Global leader in generic APIs (naproxen, gabapentin, dextromethorphan and others) and custom synthesis for big pharma, including peptides and GLP-1 building blocks
strengths: Custom synthesis grew 45% YoY in Q1 FY27 on dedicated big-pharma projects; EBITDA margin ~41%
Large net-cash balance sheet and clean USFDA record
Integrated peptide platform positioned for GLP-1 demand and BIOSECURE shifts
risks: Validation-batch revenue is lumpy - margin spike in Q1 FY27 may not repeat
Valuation already prices in CDMO success
Customer concentration in custom synthesis

laurus.name: Laurus Labs
laurus.role: API maker (ARVs, oncology, CVS) turning into a CDMO (Laurus Synthesis) with formulations and Laurus Bio
strengths: CDMO-led recovery: FY26 profit ₹890 Cr vs ₹162 Cr in FY24
Large chemistry capacity in Visakhapatnam; stock more than doubled in the year to Oct 2026
risks: ARV API pricing depends on global tenders
Very rich valuation leaves no margin for CDMO delays
Customer concentration in large CDMO contracts

aartiDrugs.name: Aarti Drugs
aartiDrugs.role: High-volume API maker (metformin, ciprofloxacin, antifungals) backward-integrated into its own intermediates
strengths: Backward integration into intermediates lowers China dependence
Lower valuation than most API peers
risks: Commodity APIs directly exposed to Chinese price competition - revenue flat FY22-FY26
Thin margins, and the stock has fallen in the year to Oct 2026

solara.name: Solara Active Pharma Sciences
solara.role: API maker (ibuprofen among the world's largest, plus anti-infectives and CNS) spun out of the Strides group
strengths: Large regulated-market API franchise and turnaround plan with CRAMS push
risks: Repeated losses (FY24 loss of ₹567 Cr with write-offs) and weak returns
Ibuprofen price competition from China

concord.name: Concord Biotech
concord.role: Fermentation-based APIs - a global leader in immunosuppressants (mycophenolate, tacrolimus) and anti-infectives - moving into formulations
strengths: Fermentation know-how is a high entry barrier; historically ~40% EBITDA margins
Debt-free
risks: FY26 revenue fell 12% and profit 30% on pricing and customer destocking
Concentration in immunosuppressant molecules

neuland.name: Neuland Laboratories
neuland.role: Complex and peptide APIs plus custom manufacturing (CMS) for innovator molecules
strengths: Peptide and complex-chemistry capability with a growing CMS book
Strong five-year share-price gains on CMS wins
risks: CMS revenue is lumpy and tied to a few innovator molecules
High valuation after a large re-rating

iolcp.name: IOL Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals
iolcp.role: One of the world's largest ibuprofen makers, integrated back into KSMs and basic chemicals (isobutylbenzene, ethyl acetate)
strengths: Integration from basic chemicals to ibuprofen API gives cost control
Diversifying into new APIs
risks: Single-molecule (ibuprofen) concentration and Chinese pricing
Flat revenue and falling profit FY22-FY25

vinati.name: Vinati Organics
vinati.role: Specialty chemicals maker and global leader in isobutylbenzene (IBB), the key starting material for ibuprofen
strengths: Dominant global share in IBB, so ibuprofen demand anywhere pulls on Vinati
Net-cash, high-return specialty chemicals franchise
risks: Pharma is an indirect exposure - ATBS and butylphenols drive most earnings
Chemical-cycle and Chinese pricing pressure; the stock has fallen sharply in the year to Oct 2026

aartiPharma.name: Aarti Pharmalabs
aartiPharma.role: Pharma intermediates, xanthine derivatives (caffeine) and APIs, with a CDMO business
strengths: Intermediates-to-API chemistry depth inherited from Aarti Industries
CDMO adds higher-margin contract work
risks: FY26 revenue fell 14% and profit 36%
Xanthine pricing pressure from China

syngene.name: Syngene International
syngene.role: India's largest CRO/CDMO - discovery, development and manufacturing for global pharma and biotech, including biologics
strengths: Deep, long-standing relationships with global pharma (Bristol Myers Squibb, Amgen and others)
Added US biologics manufacturing (Baltimore site) and Bengaluru capacity
risks: FY26 profit fell 36% and the stock has fallen sharply in the year to Oct 2026 on weak biotech demand and large-molecule customer destocking
Biologics capacity ramp-up dilutes returns on capital

saiLife.name: Sai Life Sciences
saiLife.role: Small-molecule CRDMO serving innovator pharma and biotech from discovery to commercial supply
strengths: Fast growth: FY26 profit ₹349 Cr vs ₹6 Cr in FY22
Well placed for BIOSECURE-driven vendor diversification
risks: Very rich valuation (see the figures)
Biotech funding sensitivity and customer concentration

anthem.name: Anthem Biosciences
anthem.role: Bengaluru CRDMO covering small molecules, peptides, oligos and fermentation-based specialty ingredients
strengths: Very high margins and ROCE for a CRDMO
Profit up 31% in FY26
risks: Listed only in Jul 2025 - short public track record
Revenue concentrated in a few late-stage/commercial molecules

cohance.name: Cohance Lifesciences
cohance.role: CDMO formed from Suven Pharmaceuticals and Cohance (Advent-backed), with NJ Bio adding antibody-drug-conjugate (ADC) services
strengths: Combined CDMO + specialty chemicals platform with ADC capability
risks: USFDA warning letter at its Nacharam formulation site (Feb 2026)
FY26 profit fell to ₹150 Cr; the stock has fallen sharply in the year to Oct 2026
Integration of several acquisitions

dishman.name: Dishman Carbogen Amcis
dishman.role: CDMO for high-potency APIs and late-stage/commercial molecules via Swiss subsidiary Carbogen Amcis
strengths: Swiss/European CDMO footprint valued by Western customers seeking non-China supply
risks: Weak profitability (very low ROE) and impairments
High-cost European operations

hikal.name: Hikal
hikal.role: CDMO and API maker serving pharma and crop-protection innovators
strengths: Long relationships with global innovators in both pharma and agrochemicals
risks: FY26 net loss on crop-protection weakness and pharma CDMO delays
Low returns on capital

akums.name: Akums Drugs & Pharmaceuticals
akums.role: India's largest contract manufacturer of formulations for domestic pharma brands, plus trade generics and APIs
strengths: Makes formulations for most large Indian branded companies - a toll on India market growth
Scale advantage as Revised Schedule M squeezes small contract makers
risks: API segment losses and low ROE
Margin pressure from customer pricing

glaxo.name: GSK Pharmaceuticals
glaxo.role: GSK's Indian arm selling branded medicines (Augmentin, Calpol, T-Bact) and vaccines, now adding specialty and oncology drugs
strengths: Market-leading anti-infective and pain brands
Debt-free with high return on capital
risks: Price controls on essential medicines cap many of its brands
Narrow portfolio after years of pruning

pfizerIndia.name: Pfizer India
pfizerIndia.role: Indian arm of Pfizer selling long-standing branded medicines (Becosules, Gelusil, Dolonex) and hospital products
strengths: Old, trusted brands with strong doctor recall
Debt-free with large cash reserves
risks: The parent's global priorities limit new launches in India
Price controls and slow growth in older brands

emcure.name: Emcure Pharmaceuticals
emcure.role: Pune drugmaker selling branded medicines in India (gynaecology, cardiac, anti-infectives) and a wide injectables range (iron, oncology), with generics in Europe and Canada
strengths: Strong positions in women's health and injectables
Mix of Indian brands and regulated-market exports
risks: Part of its Indian range is in-licensed from other drugmakers
Price controls on essential medicines

rubicon.name: Rubicon Research
rubicon.role: Develops and makes niche generic formulations (oral solids, liquids, nasal sprays) for the US; listed Oct 2025
strengths: Large pipeline of US approvals in limited-competition products
Fast growth from new launches
risks: Almost all sales are in the US, where generic prices fall over time
US FDA inspection outcomes at its plants

strides.name: Strides Pharma Science
strides.role: Makes oral generics for the US and other regulated markets from plants in Bengaluru and Chennai
strengths: Broad US portfolio with regular new approvals
Leaner after demerging its CDMO arm into OneSource
risks: US generic price erosion
Regulatory inspection risk

marksans.name: Marksans Pharma
marksans.role: Makes over-the-counter and generic oral medicines for the US, UK and Australia, selling largely to retail chains
strengths: OTC focus with steady retail demand
Own front-end companies in the UK and Australia
risks: Depends on a few large retail customers
Price pressure in US generics

onesource.name: OneSource Specialty Pharma
onesource.role: Bengaluru CDMO making biologics, drug-device combinations (GLP-1 pens and cartridges) and soft-gels for global drugmakers; demerged from Strides
strengths: Early capacity for GLP-1 cartridges as semaglutide patents expire
Rare mix of biologics, sterile fill-finish and soft-gel
risks: Still loss-making while new capacity fills
A few large contracts drive results

jubilantPharmova.name: Jubilant Pharmova
jubilantPharmova.role: Runs a sterile injectables CDMO with plants in the US and Canada, plus API and radiopharmaceutical businesses
strengths: One of few listed Indian sterile fill-finish CDMOs with North American plants
Strong US positions in radiopharma
risks: US FDA inspections at its sterile plants
Several businesses competing for capital

alivus.name: Alivus Life Sciences
alivus.role: Makes active pharmaceutical ingredients for chronic therapies (cardiac, diabetes, CNS); formerly Glenmark Life Sciences, now owned by Nirma
strengths: Large API portfolio with regulated-market approvals
High margins and little debt
risks: Glenmark is still a large customer
Price pressure from Chinese API makers

blueJet.name: Blue Jet Healthcare
blueJet.role: Makes intermediates for iodinated contrast media, sold to global imaging majors, plus high-intensity sweeteners such as saccharin
strengths: Long ties with the few global contrast-media makers
Deep chemistry in a niche few can supply
risks: Heavy dependence on a handful of customers
Plants concentrated in Maharashtra

apolloHosp.name: Apollo Hospitals Enterprise
apolloHosp.role: India's largest private hospital group by revenue, plus Apollo HealthCo (India's largest pharmacy network, Keimed distribution and the Apollo 24/7 app) and Apollo Health & Lifestyle (clinics, diagnostics, Cradle)
strengths: Largest pan-India network with strong brand pull for high-acuity care and international patients
Integrated model: hospitals, pharmacies, distribution, diagnostics and digital feed each other
HealthCo is being demerged into Apollo Healthtech with a separate listing targeted for Q4 FY27 - unlocks value and makes the hospital business a cleaner story
risks: Hospital occupancy dipped as new units opened (FY26); new beds take time to fill
A hospital medicine-margin cap from the Supreme Court case would hit both hospital pharmacy and retail
Demerger execution and continued Apollo 24/7 investment

maxHealth.name: Max Healthcare Institute
maxHealth.role: North India-focused super-specialty hospital chain (Delhi NCR, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Lucknow, Mumbai) with the sector's highest occupancy and revenue per bed among large chains
strengths: Q2 FY27 gross revenue rose ~20% and network profit ~10% on higher bed occupancy (company results, Oct 2026)
Large brownfield-led bed expansion on existing campuses lowers ramp-up risk
International patient revenue grew 33% in Q2 FY27
risks: Government-scheme exposure (CGHS/ECHS) means rate changes cut both ways
Heavy bed additions to FY28 may dilute margins while they fill
Rich valuation leaves little room for slips - see the figures

manipal.name: Manipal Health Enterprises (Manipal Hospitals)
manipal.role: India's largest hospital network by beds (~13,000 licensed, 49 hospitals) and No. 2 by revenue; leads Bengaluru, Kolkata and Pune; listed Aug 2026
strengths: Scale and metro leadership built through Columbia Asia, AMRI, Medica and Sahyadri acquisitions
~13,000 licensed beds across 49 hospitals (Mar 2026) give room to add capacity on existing campuses
Most of the ~₹8,000 Cr fresh issue repays group borrowings; part buys out minority holders in Sahyadri Hospitals
risks: Karnataka still brings close to half of revenue
Leverage and integration of Sahyadri and other acquired hospitals
Trades at a premium to listed peers - see the figures

fortis.name: Fortis Healthcare
fortis.role: Pan-India hospital chain promoted by Malaysia's IHH Healthcare, plus Agilus Diagnostics (~89% owned), one of India's largest pathology networks
strengths: Margin recovery under IHH: hospital EBITDA margins have risen steadily since FY22
Bolt-on acquisitions add beds in core clusters - Shrimann (Jalandhar, 2025) and People Tree (Bengaluru, agreed Dec 2025, ₹430 Cr)
Higher government-scheme share made it one of the expected gainers from the Oct 2025 CGHS revision (Nuvama)
risks: Legacy litigation from the former promoters and IHH's pending open offer
Agilus diagnostics faces the same price competition as other lab chains
Older hospitals need refurbishment capex

medanta.name: Global Health (Medanta)
medanta.role: High-acuity super-specialty hospitals under the Medanta brand - Gurugram flagship plus Lucknow, Patna, Indore, Ranchi and a new Noida hospital
strengths: Clinical reputation in transplants, cardiac and neuro sciences drives high ARPOB
Lucknow and Patna show the model works in under-served state capitals
Strong balance sheet funding the next wave of hospitals
risks: Gurugram flagship still a large share of profit
New Noida and pipeline hospitals weigh on margins while they ramp up
Doctor-led brand: retaining senior clinicians is critical

narayana.name: Narayana Hrudayalaya (Narayana Health)
narayana.role: Value-focused hospital chain known for high-volume cardiac surgery, with hospitals across India, Health City Cayman Islands, the UK's Practice Plus Group Hospitals (bought Nov 2025) and its own health-insurance arm
strengths: Low-cost, high-volume clinical model keeps prices affordable while earning good margins
Cayman Islands hospital earns in US dollars; the £188.78m Practice Plus deal adds UK elective surgery (NHS-funded)
Launched Narayana Health Insurance to sell its own integrated cover - a step toward a payer-provider model
risks: Overseas expansion adds currency, NHS-policy and integration risk
Insurance arm is small and early-stage, and needs capital before it earns
India growth depends on filling newer hospitals

kims.name: Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences (KIMS Hospitals)
kims.role: Hyderabad-based multi-specialty chain leading in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, now expanding into Karnataka, Maharashtra and Kerala
strengths: Dominant position and low-cost model in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh
Track record of turning around acquired hospitals
Large bed pipeline in new states doubles the network over a few years
risks: New-state hospitals (Bengaluru, Nashik, Thane, Kerala) dilute margins in early years
Higher share of government-scheme patients in Andhra Pradesh
Not to be confused with KIMSHEALTH (Kerala), now part of Aster DM Quality Care

asterDm.name: Aster DM Quality Care
asterDm.role: Merged hospital group (Aster DM Healthcare + Blackstone-backed Quality Care India, effective 1 Jul 2026) running Aster, CARE Hospitals, KIMSHEALTH and Evercare across south and central India
strengths: Merger creates one of India's three largest chains (~10,600 beds per ICICI Securities) with a 15,000-bed target by FY30
Strong positions in Kerala, Karnataka, Hyderabad and Andhra Pradesh
Gulf business was separated in 2024, leaving a pure India hospital play
risks: Integration of four brands and two management teams
Blackstone and the founding family share control - board and governance transitions
New-bed ramp-up and acquisition goodwill

jupiter.name: Jupiter Life Line Hospitals
jupiter.role: Western India multi-specialty chain (Thane, Pune, Indore, Dombivli) focused on tertiary and quaternary care
strengths: Mature Thane and Pune hospitals with high occupancy
Net-cash balance sheet after the 2023 IPO funds new hospitals
Focused on high-acuity specialties in a well-insured catchment
risks: Small network - each new hospital is a large share of earnings
New Dombivli and Pune capacity dilutes margins while ramping up
Competition from larger chains entering Mumbai and Pune

yatharth.name: Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services
yatharth.role: NCR and western UP hospital chain (Noida, Greater Noida, Noida Extension, Faridabad, Jhansi, Agra) serving value-conscious and government-scheme patients
strengths: Fast bed growth through acquisitions of hospitals in tier-2 cities (Agra, Faridabad)
High share of CGHS/ECHS and scheme patients made it a direct gainer from the Oct 2025 CGHS rate revision
Low cost per bed versus metro chains
risks: Lower ARPOB than metro super-specialty chains
Government receivables stretch working capital
Acquired hospitals need upgrading before they earn like the core units

paras.name: Paras Healthcare
paras.role: North India and Bihar hospital chain (Gurugram, Patna, Darbhanga, Ranchi, Panchkula, Udaipur, Kanpur, Srinagar); listed on 28 Oct 2026
strengths: Early mover in under-served state capitals and tier-2 cities, especially Bihar
Turned profitable in FY26 as newer hospitals matured (DRHP)
IPO money reduces debt
risks: Newly listed (Oct 2026) - short public track record
Loss-making years until FY26; margins below metro peers
High share of government-scheme patients in Bihar and Jharkhand

parkMedi.name: Park Medi World
parkMedi.role: Haryana-centred hospital chain (Park Hospital) with hospitals in Delhi NCR, Haryana, Punjab and Rajasthan; listed Dec 2025
strengths: Large bed base in tier-2 north Indian towns at low cost per bed
Empanelled with most government schemes, keeping beds full
IPO-funded expansion and debt reduction
risks: Government-scheme heavy mix means lower ARPOB and slower payments
Short listed history (Dec 2025)
Expansion into new states

rainbow.name: Rainbow Children's Medicare
rainbow.role: Paediatric and obstetric (mother & child) hospital chain built on a hub-and-spoke model, strongest in Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Chennai
strengths: Leader in paediatric intensive care (NICU/PICU), a skill few hospitals have
Hub-and-spoke model lets spokes refer complex cases to the hub
Net-cash balance sheet
risks: Falling birth rates cap the obstetrics market
Paediatric volumes are seasonal (monsoon/winter infections)
New-city expansion (north and east India) has lower early returns

drAgarwal.name: Dr Agarwal's Health Care
drAgarwal.role: India's largest eye-care chain (Dr Agarwal's Eye Hospitals) with centres across India and in Africa; listed Feb 2025
