Bajaj Finance must cut its stake over time to meet public-float rules

lichf.name: LIC Housing Finance
lichf.role: One of the largest housing finance companies, promoted by LIC, lending mostly to salaried buyers
strengths: LIC parentage and wide reach
Large, granular home-loan book
risks: Spread pressure from banks
Developer-loan legacy

pnbHousing.name: PNB Housing Finance
pnbHousing.role: Large HFC promoted by PNB, growing in affordable and emerging-market loans after a clean-up
strengths: Cleaned-up corporate book
Growth in affordable and self-employed segments
risks: Management transition (2025)
Competition with banks

canFinHomes.name: Can Fin Homes
canFinHomes.role: Canara Bank-promoted HFC for salaried home buyers, strongest in south India
strengths: Low-cost operations and long record
Canara Bank parentage
risks: Southern concentration
Thin spreads

pfc.name: Power Finance Corporation
pfc.role: Largest power-sector lender and REC's parent, funding generation, transmission, distribution and renewables
strengths: Near-sovereign borrowing cost
Grows with India's power capex
risks: Concentrated exposure to state discoms and private gencos
Bond-market cost when rates rise

rec.name: REC
rec.role: State power lender to utilities and nodal agency for the RDSS distribution scheme; a PFC subsidiary
strengths: Government-backed borrowing
Diversifying into infrastructure beyond power
risks: State-discom exposure
Policy on dividends and lending targets

irfc.name: Indian Railway Finance Corporation
irfc.role: Financing arm of Indian Railways that borrows and leases rolling stock and assets to the Railways at a cost-plus spread
strengths: Near-zero credit risk: the Railways is its main borrower
Funding cost passed through
risks: Growth depends on how much the Railways borrows
Thin, fixed spread

ireda.name: Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency
ireda.role: Government lender for solar, wind, hydro, storage and green-hydrogen projects; listed Nov 2023
strengths: Direct play on renewable capex
Government ownership lowers funding cost
risks: Project risk in new technologies
Stress in some solar and wind developers

hudco.name: Housing and Urban Development Corporation
hudco.role: State lender to housing boards, urban bodies and infrastructure agencies
strengths: Grows with state urban and housing capex
Government guarantee on much of its book
risks: Concentration in state-government agencies
Policy-driven lending

ifci.name: IFCI
ifci.role: Legacy government development lender, now small; the government is consolidating its subsidiaries
strengths: Government support
risks: Weak legacy loan book
Shrinking core lending

rbi.name: Reserve Bank of India
rbi.role: Central bank and regulator: sets the repo rate, licenses and supervises banks and NBFCs, and sets capital and risk-weight rules
strengths: Raised the repo rate to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026 and turned to 'calibrated tightening'
risks: Not investable - every lender's cost and growth turn on its decisions
notes: Publishes the Financial Stability Report each June and December

nabard.name: NABARD
nabard.role: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development: refinances farm and rural lending by banks, co-operatives and MFIs
strengths: Main refinance source for rural credit
risks: Unlisted, government-owned

sidbi.name: SIDBI
sidbi.role: Small Industries Development Bank of India: refinances banks, NBFCs and MFIs that lend to small businesses
strengths: Key funding source for MSME-focused NBFCs and MFIs
risks: Unlisted, government-controlled
notes: Owned by the government and public-sector institutions

nhb.name: National Housing Bank
nhb.role: Refinances housing finance companies and runs housing schemes
strengths: Cheap refinance for affordable HFCs
risks: Unlisted
notes: Wholly owned by the government since 2019 (previously RBI)

nabfid.name: NaBFID
nabfid.role: National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development: long-term infrastructure lender set up in 2021
strengths: Long-tenor funding for infrastructure
risks: Unlisted; still building its book

narcl.name: National Asset Reconstruction Company
narcl.role: Government-backed 'bad bank' that buys large stressed loans from banks, with security receipts guaranteed by the government
strengths: Clears large bad loans off bank balance sheets
risks: Unlisted; slow recoveries so far
notes: Set up 2021, majority-owned by public-sector banks

edelweiss.name: Edelweiss Financial Services
edelweiss.role: Owns Edelweiss ARC, one of the largest private asset reconstruction companies, plus credit, alternatives and insurance businesses
strengths: ARC earns from buying and resolving bad loans
Alternatives business with fee income
risks: Bad-loan supply is low while banks are healthy
RBI scrutiny of group structures (2024)

cibil.name: TransUnion CIBIL
cibil.role: India's largest credit bureau; its score is checked on almost every retail loan application
strengths: Data on most Indian borrowers
risks: Unlisted (owned by TransUnion)
notes: Experian, CRIF High Mark and Equifax are the other three bureaus

npci.name: NPCI
npci.role: National Payments Corporation of India: runs UPI, RuPay and NACH e-mandates that collect most EMIs
strengths: Owns the rails behind UPI and EMI collection
risks: Unlisted, owned by banks
notes: Not-for-profit, promoted by RBI and IBA

pineLabs.name: Pine Labs
pineLabs.role: Merchant payments leader whose card machines offer brand and bank EMIs at the point of sale; listed Nov 2025
strengths: Leader in point-of-sale EMI for brands
Issuing software for banks
risks: Depends on lenders' appetite for consumer EMIs
Competition in payments

ofss.name: Oracle Financial Services Software
ofss.role: Maker of Flexcube core banking and other banking software used by Indian and global banks
strengths: Installed base in many banks
Debt-free and pays large dividends
risks: Most revenue comes from overseas banks
Long, lumpy deal cycles

nucleus.name: Nucleus Software Exports
nucleus.role: Maker of FinnOne loan-management and FinnAxia transaction-banking software used by Indian banks and NBFCs
strengths: Long-standing NBFC and bank client base
risks: Small company with lumpy deals
Competition from larger vendors

intellect.name: Intellect Design Arena
intellect.role: Banking software maker (core banking, transaction banking, insurance) selling to Indian and global banks
strengths: Modern, modular banking products
risks: Long sales cycles
Global clients weigh more than Indian ones

tcs.name: Tata Consultancy Services
tcs.role: IT services leader whose BaNCS software runs core banking and payments at several banks
strengths: BaNCS and large bank IT contracts
risks: Banking software is a small part of a large IT business

infy.name: Infosys
infy.role: IT services leader whose Finacle core-banking software runs many Indian banks
strengths: Finacle's installed base in Indian banks
risks: Finacle is a small part of a large IT business

tataInvest.name: Tata Investment Corporation
tataInvest.role: RBI-registered investment company that holds stakes in Tata group and other listed companies
strengths: Tata group backing
No borrowing
risks: Earnings depend on dividends and stake sales
Trades at a holding-company discount

federalBank.name: Federal Bank
federalBank.role: Kerala-based private bank that co-owns Ageas Federal Life and sells its policies to depositors and NRI customers
strengths: Kerala branch and NRI customer base feeds the insurer's bank sales
Holds a stake in a life insurer partnered with Ageas of Belgium
risks: Minority holding: Ageas leads the insurer
Customers are concentrated in Kerala

pnb.name: Punjab National Bank
pnb.role: Co-owner of PNB MetLife and one of its main sellers through a large north-India branch network
strengths: Branch reach in north India supports PNB MetLife's bank sales
Holds a stake in a life insurer
risks: Minority holding: MetLife leads the insurer
Insurance is a small part of a large bank

bankOfIndia.name: Bank of India
bankOfIndia.role: Co-promoter of Star Union Dai-ichi Life with Union Bank of India and Dai-ichi Life, selling its policies through branches
strengths: Branch and overseas customer base feeds the insurer's bank sales
Holds a stake in a life insurer
risks: Minority holding: Dai-ichi Life leads the insurer
Insurance is a small part of a large bank

unionBank.name: Union Bank of India
unionBank.role: Co-promoter of Star Union Dai-ichi Life with Bank of India and Dai-ichi Life, and a seller of its policies through branches
strengths: National branch network feeds the insurer's bank sales
Holds a stake in a life insurer
risks: Minority holding: Dai-ichi Life leads the insurer
Insurance is a small part of a large bank

bankOfBaroda.name: Bank of Baroda
bankOfBaroda.role: Public-sector bank that owns a controlling stake in IndiaFirst Life and sells its policies through its branches
strengths: Wide branch network is IndiaFirst Life's main sales channel
Holds control of a life insurer
risks: Insurance is a small part of a large bank
Public-sector cross-sell is slower than at private banks

edelweiss.name: Edelweiss Financial Services
edelweiss.role: Parent of Edelweiss Life and Zuno General, two insurers inside a group better known for credit, wealth and asset reconstruction
strengths: Owns both a life and a general insurer
Wealth and credit clients are a ready customer base for cross-sell
risks: Both insurers are small beside the private-sector leaders and may need more capital
Insurance is a minor part of group figures that mix credit, alternatives and asset reconstruction

cholaHoldings.name: Cholamandalam Financial Holdings
cholaHoldings.role: Murugappa group holding company that owns the group's stake in Cholamandalam MS General Insurance beside its lending arm
strengths: Look-through exposure to a general insurer run with Mitsui Sumitomo
Group lending customers are a ready base for motor and property cover
risks: Holding-company discount; the lending arm dominates group value
The insurer's profit reaches it only as dividends or growth in value

sbi.name: State Bank of India
sbi.role: Promoter of SBI Life and SBI General; its branches are SBI Life's main sales channel
strengths: Widest branch network in India sells SBI Life's policies at the lowest distribution cost
Its stake in SBI Life is one of its most valuable subsidiaries
risks: Insurance is a small part of a very large bank's earnings
Mis-selling scrutiny on policies sold to depositors

hdfcBank.name: HDFC Bank
hdfcBank.role: Promoter of HDFC Life and HDFC ERGO and the largest bancassurance partner of HDFC Life
strengths: Large affluent customer base for protection and savings policies
Owns both a life and a general insurer
risks: HDFC Life also sells through other banks, and HDFC Bank sells other insurers' policies
Insurance is a minor part of bank-level figures

icicibank.name: ICICI Bank
icicibank.role: Controlling shareholder of ICICI Life and ICICI Lombard; sells both through its branches and app
strengths: Owns a leading life insurer and the largest private general insurer
Strong digital cross-sell to retail and business customers
risks: Bank figures dominate; insurance value is in subsidiaries
Group insurers also compete for the same customers with other banks' partners

axisbank.name: Axis Bank
axisbank.role: Co-owner (about a fifth) of Axis Max Life and its main bancassurance channel
strengths: Branch and card base drives Axis Max Life's banca sales
Option to raise its stake in the insurer (discussed in 2026)
risks: Minority stake: most of the insurer's value goes to Max Financial
Insurance is a small part of the bank's figures

kotak.name: Kotak Mahindra Bank
kotak.role: Owns Kotak Mahindra Life outright and a minority of Zurich Kotak General; sells both through branches
strengths: Wholly owns its life insurer
Affluent customers suit protection and savings policies
risks: Life insurer is unlisted; its value is buried in bank figures
Sold control of the general insurer to Zurich (2024)

canaraBank.name: Canara Bank
canaraBank.role: Promoter of listed Canara HSBC Life and its main distribution partner
strengths: Large public-sector branch network in the south and in smaller towns
Holds a listed stake in Canara HSBC Life
risks: Insurance is a small part of a large bank
Public-sector bank cross-sell is slower than private peers'

pbFintech.name: PB Fintech (PolicyBazaar, Paisabazaar)
pbFintech.role: India's largest online insurance marketplace, strongest in term life and retail health, with renewal income building each year
strengths: Dominant share of online term and health sales
Renewals give a growing recurring base
Call-centre-assisted model converts first-time buyers
risks: Bima Sugam and insurers' own apps could cut the take rate
IRDAI commission and expense-of-management rules
Heavy marketing spend

turtlemint.name: Turtlemint Fintech Solutions
turtlemint.role: Platform that lets independent agents and point-of-sale persons quote and sell motor, health and life policies from many insurers
strengths: Agent-tech model reaches small-town buyers who want advice
Multi-insurer, multi-line catalogue
risks: Listed only on 29 Jun 2026; short public track record
Motor-heavy commissions are thin and price-sensitive

insuranceDekho.name: InsuranceDekho
insuranceDekho.role: Online and agent-led insurance broker from the Girnar (CarDekho) group
strengths: Strong in motor insurance through the CarDekho car-buying funnel
risks: Unlisted; IPO plans reported in 2026 but not confirmed filed

prudent.name: Prudent Corporate Advisory Services
prudent.role: Mutual-fund distribution platform with a growing insurance-broking arm selling through its distributor network
strengths: Tens of thousands of distributors can cross-sell insurance
Strong in smaller towns
risks: Insurance is a small share of its income; mutual-fund trail dominates

hdfclife.name: HDFC Life Insurance
hdfclife.role: Large private life insurer; HDFC Bank and other banks sell 58% of its individual policies (H1 FY27)
strengths: Balanced product mix across protection, non-par, par, ULIP and annuity
Many bank partners beyond HDFC Bank, plus agency
risks: Persistency slipped in H1 FY27 (13th month 83% vs 86%, company)
Commission and surrender-value rules and loss of GST input credit

sbilife.name: SBI Life Insurance
sbilife.role: SBI-promoted life insurer selling mainly through State Bank branches
strengths: Lowest-cost distribution in the industry via SBI's branches
Among the highest value-of-new-business returns of the large listed life insurers (company)
risks: Heavy reliance on a single bank channel
ULIP-heavy mix swings with equity markets

iciciLife.name: ICICI Life Insurance
iciciLife.role: ICICI Bank-controlled life insurer (formerly ICICI Prudential Life), strong in protection and ULIPs
strengths: Retail protection and annuity growth; VNB grew 22.3% in H1 FY27 (company)
13th-month persistency of 84.5% (H1 FY27, company)
risks: Savings APE grew slowly (6.6% in H1 FY27)
Renamed and re-symbolled in Oct 2026 - check old-name data

maxFinancial.name: Max Financial Services (Axis Max Life)
maxFinancial.role: Listed holding company of Axis Max Life Insurance (Axis Bank entities own the rest); its value is almost entirely the life insurer
strengths: Balanced agency and Axis Bank banca distribution
VNB grew 21% in H1 FY27 and embedded value 17% (company)
risks: Holding-company structure; Axis Bank may raise its stake
Solvency eased over the year to Sep 2026 (company) - see the insurer figures

canaraHsbcLife.name: Canara HSBC Life Insurance
canaraHsbcLife.role: Canara Bank-HSBC life insurer selling mainly through Canara Bank branches; listed 17 Oct 2025
strengths: Captive public-sector branch network
HSBC's product and risk know-how
risks: Smaller scale than the large bank-led peers
Dependence on one public-sector bank

indiaFirstLife.name: IndiaFirst Life Insurance
indiaFirstLife.role: Bank of Baroda- and Union Bank-promoted life insurer selling through their branches
strengths: Two public-sector bank partners
risks: Unlisted; earlier IPO filing did not lead to a listing

lic.name: Life Insurance Corporation of India
lic.role: State-owned market leader: 58.77% of first-year premium in H1 FY27 and most group life and pension business (company)
strengths: Largest agency force and brand trust in rural India
Embedded value larger than all listed private life insurers combined
risks: Mostly participating policies, so a lower VNB margin than private peers
Government ownership and future stake sales

bajajLife.name: Bajaj Life Insurance
bajajLife.role: Bajaj group's life insurer (formerly Bajaj Allianz Life), wholly Bajaj-owned after Allianz's exit in 2026
strengths: Fast-growing agency and bank partnerships
Full control lets the group set strategy alone
risks: Unlisted; held through Bajaj Finserv and Bajaj Holdings
notes: Unlisted - exposure through BAJAJFINSV and BAJAJHLDNG

tataAiaLife.name: Tata AIA Life Insurance
tataAiaLife.role: Tata Sons-AIA joint venture; a large seller of protection and ULIPs
strengths: Strong protection franchise and AIA's know-how
risks: No listed proxy (Tata Sons is unlisted)

abslInsurance.name: Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance
abslInsurance.role: Life arm of Aditya Birla Capital, a joint venture with Sun Life
strengths: Group cross-sell across lending, AMC and health insurance
risks: Mid-sized player; exposure only via ABCAPITAL

kotakLife.name: Kotak Mahindra Life Insurance
kotakLife.role: Life insurer wholly owned by Kotak Mahindra Bank
strengths: Bank parent's affluent customers
risks: Unlisted; value sits inside Kotak Mahindra Bank

pnbMetLife.name: PNB MetLife India Insurance
pnbMetLife.role: MetLife-led life insurer with Punjab National Bank as partner and distributor
strengths: PNB's branch network
risks: Unlisted; minority bank partner

iciciLombard.name: ICICI Lombard General Insurance
iciciLombard.role: Largest private general insurer across motor, health, fire and engineering, selling through ICICI Bank, agents, brokers and online
strengths: Diversified book and large reinsurance and catastrophe protection
Reports a combined ratio excluding catastrophe losses, making trends easier to read
risks: Motor third-party claims inflation before any premium revision
Flood losses lifted the Q2 FY27 combined ratio (company)

newIndia.name: New India Assurance
newIndia.role: Largest general insurer by premium (government-owned), with the biggest health and commercial books
strengths: Largest premium base and pan-India reach
Large investment portfolio built over decades
risks: Underwriting losses in motor third-party, group health and property
Solvency headroom over the 1.5x regulatory minimum is thin for an insurer of its size

goDigit.name: Go Digit General Insurance
goDigit.role: Digital-first private general insurer, mostly motor, selling through agents, brokers and partner apps
strengths: Low-cost digital operations and fast growth
Underwriting near break-even on its reported CISR (Q2 FY27, company)
risks: Motor-heavy book exposed to third-party claims
Reports several combined-ratio bases - compare with care

bajajGeneral.name: Bajaj General Insurance
bajajGeneral.role: Bajaj group's general insurer (formerly Bajaj Allianz General), wholly Bajaj-owned after Allianz's exit
strengths: Among the most profitable private general insurers historically
risks: Unlisted; exposure only via Bajaj Finserv and Bajaj Holdings
notes: Unlisted - exposure through BAJAJFINSV and BAJAJHLDNG

hdfcErgo.name: HDFC ERGO General Insurance
hdfcErgo.role: HDFC Bank's general insurer with large retail health and motor books
strengths: HDFC Bank distribution
risks: Unlisted; value inside HDFC Bank

tataAig.name: Tata AIG General Insurance
tataAig.role: Tata Sons-AIG joint venture, strong in commercial lines and motor
strengths: Commercial and specialty underwriting skill from AIG
risks: No listed proxy

starHealth.name: Star Health and Allied Insurance
starHealth.role: India's largest standalone health insurer, focused on retail policies sold through agents
strengths: Largest retail health book and agency network
Underwriting profit in Q2 FY27, its fifth straight quarter of improvement (company)
risks: Claims inflation from hospital price rises
Share loss to multi-line insurers and Niva Bupa

nivaBupa.name: Niva Bupa Health Insurance
nivaBupa.role: Standalone health insurer promoted by the UK's Bupa (formerly Max Bupa), gaining retail health share
strengths: Fast premium growth through banks and online
Bupa's global health-insurance know-how
risks: Profitability is still young; Q2 is seasonally weak
Ind AS vs Indian GAAP profit gaps confuse comparisons

careHealth.name: Care Health Insurance
careHealth.role: Standalone health insurer, a subsidiary of listed Religare Enterprises
strengths: One of the top standalone health insurers by retail premium
risks: Unlisted itself; parent Religare saw a control change in 2025
notes: No listed market data for the insurer

adityaBirlaHealth.name: Aditya Birla Health Insurance
adityaBirlaHealth.role: Health insurance arm of Aditya Birla Capital, focused on wellness-linked retail policies
strengths: Wellness rewards and group cross-sell
risks: Unlisted; exposure only via ABCAPITAL

manipalCigna.name: ManipalCigna Health Insurance
strengths: Hospital-group parentage
risks: Reported stake talks with LIC (2024-25) not confirmed closed

gicRe.name: General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re)
gicRe.role: State-owned national reinsurer; receives a statutory share of every Indian general policy and leads most domestic treaties
strengths: Dominant domestic reinsurer with statutory business
Very high solvency and a large investment book
risks: Catastrophe and crop losses swing results
New private reinsurers and foreign branches compete for treaties

allianzJioRe.name: Allianz Jio Reinsurance
allianzJioRe.role: 50:50 Allianz-Jio Financial reinsurer registered by IRDAI in Mar 2026, the second private Indian reinsurer
strengths: Allianz's global reinsurance expertise with Jio's capital
risks: New entrant building a book in a market anchored by GIC Re

munichReIndia.name: Munich Re (India branch)
munichReIndia.role: Foreign reinsurer branch in India competing with GIC Re for treaty and large-risk business
strengths: Global capacity and pricing data
risks: Branch capital and statutory cession rules favour GIC Re

swissReIndia.name: Swiss Re (India branch)
swissReIndia.role: Foreign reinsurer branch in India writing treaty, life and specialty reinsurance
strengths: Global capacity and life reinsurance expertise
risks: Competes with GIC Re's statutory advantage

mediAssist.name: Medi Assist Healthcare Services
mediAssist.role: India's largest third-party administrator (TPA) - processes cashless and reimbursement claims for insurers and employers
strengths: Scale leader; bought Paramount TPA (Jul 2025)
Revenue grows with group health premiums under management
risks: Insurers bringing claims processing in-house
Fee pressure; regulatory changes to TPA roles

hitpa.name: Health Insurance TPA of India
hitpa.role: TPA owned by the public-sector general insurers, handling much of their group and government-scheme health claims
strengths: Captive volume from state-owned insurers
risks: Unlisted; depends on its owners' strategy

bajajfinsv.name: Bajaj Finserv
bajajfinsv.role: Holding company of Bajaj Life and Bajaj General (with Bajaj Holdings) and of Bajaj Finance
strengths: Full control of two large insurers after buying out Allianz (23% closed 8 Jan 2026)
Insurance and lending in one stock
risks: Lending (Bajaj Finance) drives the group figures
Holding-company discount

bajajHoldings.name: Bajaj Holdings & Investment
bajajHoldings.role: Bajaj group holding company with direct stakes in Bajaj Life and Bajaj General alongside Bajaj Finserv
strengths: Look-through exposure to Bajaj Finserv, Bajaj Auto and the insurers
risks: Deep holding-company discount
Insurance is one of several holdings

abCapital.name: Aditya Birla Capital
abCapital.role: Holds Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance and Aditya Birla Health Insurance alongside lending and asset management
strengths: Life, health, lending and AMC under one brand
risks: Lending drives group figures
Insurance arms are mid-sized

religare.name: Religare Enterprises
religare.role: Parent of Care Health Insurance - its main source of value
strengths: Majority stake in a large standalone health insurer
risks: Control change and governance disputes in 2025
Value depends on one unlisted subsidiary

jioFin.name: Jio Financial Services
jioFin.role: Reliance group's financial-services arm; 50% owner of Allianz Jio Reinsurance and an insurance broker
strengths: Reliance's customer reach for insurance broking
Reinsurance JV with Allianz
risks: Insurance is a very small part of the group today

irdai.name: IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India)
irdai.role: Licenses insurers and intermediaries; sets solvency (150% control level), product, commission/expense and claims rules
strengths: Clear capital rules; moving to risk-based solvency
risks: Rule changes can shift value between customers, distributors and insurers quickly

bimaSugam.name: Bima Sugam India Federation
bimaSugam.role: Not-for-profit owner of Bima Sugam, the public marketplace meant to list, sell and service every policy
strengths: Could cut acquisition cost for simple covers
risks: Repeated launch delays; motor first, life and health later

nhcx.name: National Health Claims Exchange (NHCX)
nhcx.role: Government digital exchange for health-claim messages between hospitals, TPAs and insurers
strengths: Standard claim formats can speed cashless approvals
risks: Hospital adoption is uneven

phoenix.name: The Phoenix Mills
phoenix.role: Mall owner that also owns the St. Regis Mumbai and Courtyard Agra hotels
strengths: Hotels sit beside its malls and offices, sharing footfall
Luxury Mumbai hotel under a global chain brand
risks: Hotels are a small part of a mall-led group
Hotel earnings swing with business and leisure travel

oberoi.name: Oberoi Realty
oberoi.role: Mumbai developer that owns the Westin Mumbai Garden City beside its Goregaon projects
strengths: Owns a large branded hotel inside its own township
Low-debt owner with long-held Mumbai land
risks: Hospitality is a small part of a residential-led developer's figures
Entirely Mumbai-focused

prestige.name: Prestige Estates Projects
prestige.role: Bengaluru developer whose hospitality arm owns the JW Marriott, Conrad and Sheraton hotels in the city
strengths: Owns large branded hotels on its own sites, run under global chain brands
Hotels sit beside its offices and malls
risks: Hospitality is a small part of a developer's figures
Hotels are capital-heavy and concentrated in Bengaluru

indhotel.name: Indian Hotels Company (IHCL)
indhotel.role: India's largest hotel company - Taj, Vivanta, SeleQtions, Ginger and others - with 670 hotels signed and 390 operating (Sep 2026), growing mainly through management contracts
strengths: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21% with domestic same-store RevPAR up 25%; FY27 revenue guidance raised to 15-17% (26 Oct 2026)
Pipeline of 280 hotels (32,000+ rooms), mostly capital-light management contracts, so fee income grows faster than owned rooms
Spans luxury (Taj) to economy (Ginger), plus new businesses (Qmin, amã Stays)
risks: A wave of new signings across the industry lifts supply from 2027
Event shocks (conflict, terror attacks) hit its leisure and Mumbai-heavy portfolio
Rich valuation leaves little room for slips - see the figures

itchotels.name: ITC Hotels
itchotels.role: Owner-operator of ITC's luxury hotels plus managed Welcomhotel, Storii, Fortune and Mementos brands; demerged from ITC (effective 1 Jan 2025) and listed 29 Jan 2025
strengths: Q2 FY27 revenue rose ~26% and net profit ~52%, with RevPAR up 21% (company results, Oct 2026)
Owns large flagship luxury hotels in key cities - hard-to-copy assets
Asset-light growth through managed brands
risks: ITC still holds about 40%, so a parent stake sale is an overhang
Branded-residence income is lumpy
Capex for new owned hotels and refurbishments

eihotel.name: EIH (Oberoi Hotels)
eihotel.role: Owner-operator of Oberoi and Trident hotels - the highest room rates among Indian listed hotel companies - plus flight catering and selective management contracts
strengths: Top-end Oberoi brand commands premium rates at home and abroad
Mostly owned hotels with a strong balance sheet
Flight catering adds airline-linked revenue
risks: Slow, owned-asset growth versus fee-led peers
Concentration in a few luxury markets
Large promoter and strategic holdings limit the free float

theleela.name: Leela Palaces Hotels & Resorts (formerly Schloss Bangalore)
theleela.role: Owner and operator of The Leela palaces and hotels, controlled by Brookfield; listed 2 Jun 2025
strengths: Pure luxury portfolio with high room rates in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Udaipur and other leisure spots
IPO proceeds used to repay debt
Brookfield's backing for acquisitions and management contracts
risks: Still more leveraged than older peers
Brookfield may sell down over time
Small portfolio: one weak market moves results

eihahotels.name: EIH Associated Hotels
eihahotels.role: Separately listed Oberoi-group company that owns a few Oberoi and Trident hotels, run by EIH
strengths: Owns established leisure and city hotels under Oberoi management
risks: Small, thinly traded; easily confused with EIH itself
Growth depends on the parent's decisions

lemontree.name: Lemon Tree Hotels
lemontree.role: Largest listed midscale chain (Aurika, Lemon Tree Premier, Lemon Tree, Red Fox, Keys), moving its owned hotels into Fleur Hotels to become mainly a brand and management business
strengths: Leading midscale brand with a large managed and franchised pipeline in tier-2/3 cities
Fleur reorganisation brings Warburg Pincus in (up to ₹960 Cr) and separates owned hotels from the fee business
Lower GST on rooms up to ₹7,500 suits its price points
risks: Fleur scheme still needs NCLT and shareholder approval (applied Oct 2026)

strengths: Leads toilet and floor cleaners and antiseptic liquid
risks: Unlisted

hndfds.name: Hindustan Foods
hndfds.role: India's largest contract manufacturer for FMCG brands: detergents, personal care, ice cream, foods and shoes made in its plants for HUL, Reckitt and others
strengths: Majors outsourcing capacity to it instead of building plants
Many categories and customers
risks: Thin per-unit margins
A few customers are most of revenue

shKelkar.name: S H Kelkar and Company
shKelkar.role: Largest Indian fragrance and flavour house (Keva) supplying soap, detergent, agarbatti and food makers
strengths: Fragrances written into FMCG formulas
Own aroma-chemical plants
risks: Global fragrance houses compete for the same briefs
European operations add risk

galaxy.name: Galaxy Surfactants
galaxy.role: Surfactants and care ingredients for shampoos, soaps, body washes and toothpastes, sold to HUL, P&G, Colgate and global FMCG makers
strengths: Long-standing FMCG customer approvals
Plants in India, Egypt and the US
risks: Fatty alcohol and ethylene oxide costs
Customer concentration

manorama.name: Manorama Industries
manorama.role: Raipur maker of cocoa butter equivalents and specialty fats from sal and shea seeds for chocolate and confectionery makers
strengths: Cheaper substitute for cocoa butter while cocoa is costly
Sal-seed collection network in central India
risks: Cocoa prices falling back
Seed supply depends on forest collection

fineOrganic.name: Fine Organic Industries
fineOrganic.role: Oleochemical maker whose emulsifiers and food additives go into bakery, snack, ice-cream and dairy products made by the brands above
strengths: Food emulsifiers sit in recipes that makers rarely reformulate
Net cash
risks: Food and cosmetic additives are one segment beside plastics and paints
Vegetable oil price swings reach its costs

privi.name: Privi Speciality Chemicals
privi.role: Aroma chemicals made from turpentine feedstock and sold to the fragrance houses that supply soap and detergent makers
strengths: Large aroma-chemical range with global fragrance-house customers
risks: Sells to fragrance houses, not to FMCG brands directly, so the link is two steps removed
Turpentine price swings and expansion debt

epl.name: EPL
epl.role: World's largest laminated-tube maker for toothpaste and cosmetics, with plants in India, China, Europe and the Americas
strengths: Long contracts with Colgate, HUL and P&G
Recyclable Platina tubes
risks: Polymer and foil costs
Few large customers

uflex.name: UFLEX
uflex.role: Polyester and polypropylene film maker and converter of printed laminates for sachets, chips bags and pouches, plus Asepto liquid cartons
strengths: Integrated from film to printed pack
Film plants abroad
risks: Global BOPET film oversupply
Debt from expansions

huhtamaki.name: Huhtamaki India
huhtamaki.role: Flexible laminates, labels and pouches for food, personal care and pharma brands
strengths: Approved supplier to large FMCG makers
risks: Resin pass-through lag
Price competition from smaller converters

tcpl.name: TCPL Packaging
tcpl.role: Folding cartons, cigarette shells and flexible packs for cigarette, food and personal-care brands
strengths: Cigarette shells and premium cartons need high print quality
risks: Cigarette volumes under tax pressure
Paperboard costs

agi.name: AGI Greenpac
agi.role: Glass bottle maker for liquor, beer, food and pharma
strengths: Large furnace capacity in north and south India
risks: Gas and soda ash costs
Liquor and beer are most of its glass demand

moldtek.name: Mold-Tek Packaging
moldtek.role: Injection-moulded pails and tubs with in-mould labels for paint, lubricant, food and FMCG makers
strengths: In-mould labelling and square pails
risks: Paint and lubricant demand is most of sales
Polypropylene costs

dmart.name: Avenue Supermarts (DMart)
dmart.role: Low-price supermarket chain whose shelf prices are the benchmark brands and apps price against
strengths: Buys direct from brands at deep discounts
Owns most of its stores
risks: Quick commerce takes top-up baskets in metros

relRetail.name: Reliance Retail
relRetail.role: Largest Indian retailer (Smart Bazaar, JioMart, Metro Cash & Carry) and B2B supplier to kiranas through JioMart Partner
strengths: Stores, wholesale and kirana network in one group
risks: Unlisted
notes: Reliance Retail Ventures, a subsidiary of Reliance Industries

eternal.name: Eternal (Zomato, Blinkit)
eternal.role: Owner of Blinkit, the largest quick-commerce app and a fast-growing FMCG sales channel in big cities
strengths: Largest dark-store network
risks: Discounting that distributors contest

swiggy.name: Swiggy
swiggy.role: Owner of Instamart, a quick-commerce app selling FMCG packs in 10-30 minutes
strengths: Moving to owned inventory, which gives brands one buyer
risks: Still loss-making in quick commerce

zepto.name: Zepto
zepto.role: Unlisted quick-commerce app and a growing FMCG sales channel in big cities
strengths: Large dark-store network
risks: Unlisted

udaan.name: Udaan
udaan.role: B2B app supplying kiranas with FMCG packs on credit
strengths: Reaches small shops brands don't cover
risks: Unlisted

jumbotail.name: Jumbotail
jumbotail.role: B2B grocery marketplace and wholesaler for kiranas
strengths: Wholesale and credit for small shops
risks: Unlisted

vmm.name: Vishal Mega Mart
vmm.role: Value hypermarket chain in tier-2 to tier-4 towns that sells groceries and FMCG packs next to apparel and home goods, mostly under its own labels
strengths: 844 stores in 582 cities (30 Sep 2026) give brands a small-town shelf outside the metros
Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14% to ₹3,399 Cr
risks: Apparel and general merchandise, not FMCG, drive most of its sales
Own labels compete with the brands on its shelves
Profit grew only about 4% in Q2 FY27

renuka.name: Shree Renuka Sugars
renuka.role: Wilmar-controlled sugar refiner and miller: refines imported raw sugar at port refineries and makes ethanol from cane and grain
strengths: Largest port-based sugar refining capacity in India
Wilmar's backing and global sourcing
risks: Has made losses for years and carries high debt
Sugar exports and ethanol prices are set by the government

dalmiaSugar.name: Dalmia Bharat Sugar
dalmiaSugar.role: Sugar miller in Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra with distilleries and cogeneration plants
strengths: Integrated sugar, ethanol and power
Lower debt than most sugar peers
risks: Cane prices and sugar export limits are set by the government
Ethanol prices are fixed by the oil marketing companies

praj.name: Praj Industries
praj.role: Engineering firm that designs and builds most of India's grain and cane ethanol distilleries, plus biogas and bio-chemical plants
strengths: Market leader in ethanol plant technology
Expanding into sustainable aviation fuel and compressed biogas
risks: New distillery orders slowed as ethanol capacity ran ahead of blending demand
Lumpy project execution

orkla.name: Orkla India
orkla.role: Packaged foods maker owning MTR (ready-to-eat, breakfast mixes) and Eastern (spices, masalas); controlled by Norway's Orkla, listed Nov 2025
strengths: Leading spice brand in Kerala and a strong MTR franchise in Karnataka
Debt-free with good cash generation
risks: Sales concentrated in South India
Spice and grain raw-material prices

cello.name: Cello World
cello.role: Sells houseware (bottles, lunch boxes, steel and glassware), writing instruments (Cello, Unomax) and moulded furniture
strengths: Strong houseware brand with wide distribution
Own glassware plant reduces reliance on imports
risks: Competition from Milton and unbranded makers
Slower growth in writing instruments

eveready.name: Eveready Industries
eveready.role: India's largest dry-cell battery and torch maker, also selling LED lighting; now makes alkaline batteries in India
strengths: Dominant battery brand in general trade
New Jammu alkaline battery plant cuts reliance on imports
risks: Competition from Duracell and Nippo
Zinc and other metal costs

lgeindia.name: LG Electronics India
lgeindia.role: India's leading maker of refrigerators, washing machines, room ACs and TVs, with plants at Noida and Pune and a third at Sri City adding its own compressors; listed 14 Oct 2025
strengths: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19.5% to ₹7,380 Cr and profit 25.7%; home appliances and air solutions up 20.9% (5 Nov 2026)
Sri City plant to make compressors from Q3 FY27 and ACs from about Jan 2027, cutting reliance on imported compressors
Leads refrigerators and front-load washers through Croma, Reliance Digital and its own brand shops
risks: Pays a royalty to LG Electronics (Korea); the parent decides product and export plans
Room-AC volumes swing with the summer
Samsung and Chinese-owned brands compete hard on price

whirlpool.name: Whirlpool of India
whirlpool.role: Refrigerator (direct-cool and frost-free) and top-load washing-machine brand with plants at Pune, Faridabad and Puducherry; the US parent holds about 40% and is looking to sell more
strengths: Strong in direct-cool refrigerators for smaller towns
Wide dealer and service network
risks: Parent's stake sale (Advent, Reliance Retail and Havells reported as bidders) leaves strategy unsettled
Lost refrigerator share to LG, Samsung and Haier
Royalty to the US parent

voltas.name: Voltas
voltas.role: Tata group's room-AC leader and air-cooler brand, with Voltbek (a JV with Turkey's Arçelik) selling refrigerators and washing machines; its projects arm is covered in Real Estate
strengths: Sold 10 lakh room ACs in the first 81 days of FY27; volumes up 45% in Q1 FY27 with about 17% market share
Tata brand and the widest AC dealer reach
risks: Very seasonal: a mild summer leaves channel stock and discounts
Compressor imports and copper costs
Voltbek still building scale in fridges and washers

bluestar.name: Blue Star
bluestar.role: Room-AC and commercial refrigeration brand (deep freezers, water coolers) with its own Sri City and Wada plants; central AC projects are covered in Real Estate
strengths: Gained room-AC share with in-house manufacturing
Commercial refrigeration for food chains and pharmacies
risks: Room-AC price war and seasonal inventory
Compressor sourcing under the BIS import limits

ifb.name: IFB Industries
ifb.role: Front-load washing-machine pioneer in India (Goa plant) adding ACs, dishwashers and kitchen appliances, plus a fine-blanking auto-parts unit
strengths: Strong in front-load washers and dishwashers in metros
risks: Small scale against LG and Samsung
AC entry has been loss-making

samsung.name: Samsung India Electronics
samsung.role: Samsung's Indian arm: refrigerators and washing machines from Chennai, ACs and TVs, and a leading appliance brand alongside LG
strengths: Strong in frost-free refrigerators, front-load washers and premium TVs
risks: Unlisted

dixon.name: Dixon Technologies
dixon.role: Contract maker of semi-automatic and fully automatic washing machines and refrigerators for brands that sell under their own labels; its phone and TV work is covered in the electronics policies
strengths: Assembles washing machines for several leading brands at scale
risks: Appliances are a small part of its revenue; brands can bring production in-house

amber.name: Amber Enterprises India
amber.role: Largest contract maker of room ACs and AC sub-assemblies (heat exchangers, motors, PCBs) for most Indian AC brands
strengths: Makes a large share of India's branded room ACs and their components
risks: Brands taking assembly in-house (LG, Blue Star)
Very seasonal order flow

crompton.name: Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals
crompton.role: India's largest ceiling-fan brand and a leading pump maker, owner of Butterfly kitchen appliances (cookers, mixers, cooktops)
strengths: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18% to ₹2,263 Cr and profit 65%; BLDC fans up about 40% and exports up 70%
Fan leadership in the BEE-rated BLDC shift
Butterfly adds a South India kitchen franchise
risks: Copper and aluminium costs in motors
Price competition in fans and lighting
Butterfly integration still to show margins

havells.name: Havells India
havells.role: Fans, water heaters, kitchen appliances and Lloyd room ACs and TVs sold to households; switchgear and wires are covered in Real Estate
strengths: Premium fan and appliance brand with its own exclusive Havells Galaxy stores
Lloyd gives it an AC and refrigerator line
risks: Lloyd has been margin-dilutive
Seasonal AC inventory

vguard.name: V-Guard Industries
vguard.role: Kerala-born brand of voltage stabilisers, water heaters, fans, pumps and Sunflame kitchen appliances, strongest in South India
strengths: Leading stabiliser and water-heater brand in the South
Expanding into North and West India
risks: Southern concentration
Wires and electricals also face copper costs

polycab.name: Polycab India
polycab.role: Wires and cables maker whose fast-moving electrical goods arm sells fans, lights, switches and appliances to households
strengths: Wire and cable dealer network gives its fans, lights and switches ready shelf space
risks: Fans, lights and switches are a small share of sales; cables drive results
Crowded against Havells, Crompton and Orient
Copper price swings

bajajelec.name: Bajaj Electricals
bajajelec.role: Fans, water heaters, mixers and cookware under Bajaj, Morphy Richards and Nirlep, plus consumer lighting; its EPC arm was demerged as Bajel Projects
strengths: Wide rural reach through distributors
Trusted Bajaj name in fans and kitchen appliances
risks: Share loss in fans to Crompton and Havells
Margin recovery still slow

orientelec.name: Orient Electric
orientelec.role: CK Birla group fan, lighting and small-appliance brand, among the leading ceiling-fan makers
strengths: Strong in premium and BLDC fans, plus exports
risks: Fans are most of its business, so summer and copper drive results

ttkprestige.name: TTK Prestige
ttkprestige.role: Prestige pressure cookers, cookware, gas stoves and kitchen appliances sold through its Prestige Xclusive stores and dealers
strengths: Leading pressure-cooker and cookware brand
Own store chain and net cash
risks: Sales have been flat for several years
Chinese and online brands in small appliances

hawkins.name: Hawkins Cookers
hawkins.role: Hawkins and Futura pressure cookers and cookware, made in-house and sold through kitchenware dealers
strengths: Premium brand in pressure cookers with high returns
risks: Narrow product range
Aluminium and steel prices

symphony.name: Symphony
symphony.role: India's leading air-cooler brand, selling in India and through Climate Technologies in Australia
strengths: Category leader in branded air coolers
Asset-light: production is outsourced
risks: Almost entirely a summer business
Room ACs replacing coolers as prices fall

welspunliv.name: Welspun Living
welspunliv.role: One of the world's largest makers of towels and bed sheets for US and UK retailers (Walmart, Target, Costco), with US pillow plants and flooring
strengths: Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 16% to ₹2,838 Cr and profit about 13-fold; home-textile exports up 18%; net cash (Oct 2026)
US pillow business grew 2.4 times in Q2 FY27
Duty-free UK access under the FTA
risks: Most sales go to the US: tariff changes hit orders
Vapi floods disrupted Q2 FY27
Cotton and freight costs

trident.name: Trident
trident.role: Punjab-based maker of cotton yarn, towels and bed linen for global retailers, plus writing and printing paper
strengths: Integrated yarn-to-towel production
Q2 FY27 profit nearly doubled to about ₹176 Cr on wider margins
risks: US retailer concentration in home textiles
Cotton price swings and paper cycle
Large planned capex

sheelafoam.name: Sheela Foam
sheelafoam.role: Sleepwell mattresses and Kurlon (bought 2023), plus PU foam for furniture and cars and a business in Australia
strengths: Largest branded mattress maker with own foam production
Kurlon adds reach in the South
risks: Foam chemicals (polyol, TDI) priced off crude
Online-first brands (Wakefit) take share

wakefit.name: Wakefit Innovations
wakefit.role: Online-first mattress, pillow and furniture brand with its own factories and a growing store chain; listed 15 Dec 2025
strengths: Low prices from direct-to-consumer sales and in-house making
Adding stores to reach offline buyers
risks: Store rollout raises fixed costs
Competition from Sheela Foam and marketplaces

nilkamal.name: Nilkamal
nilkamal.role: Plastic chairs and furniture, material-handling crates and pallets, Nilkamal mattresses and @home furniture stores
strengths: Household name in moulded furniture with wide dealer reach
risks: Polymer prices
Retail @home stores have thin margins

boschHomeComfort.name: Bosch Home Comfort India
boschHomeComfort.role: Sells Hitachi-brand room ACs (formerly Johnson Controls-Hitachi Air Conditioning India) through dealers and appliance chains
strengths: Bosch ownership brings global cooling technology and capital
risks: Small share against LG, Voltas, Daikin and Blue Star
Loss-making or near break-even in most recent years
Room-AC sales swing with summer heat

pgel.name: PG Electroplast
pgel.role: Contract maker that assembles room ACs and washing machines for appliance brands, plus plastic mouldings
strengths: Room ACs and washing machines are most of its sales, made for brands that do not own plants
Moulding and electronics capacity under one roof
risks: A few brand customers account for most orders
Summer weather swings AC orders
FY26 profit fell to ₹197 Cr despite higher revenue

pageind.name: Page Industries
pageind.role: Exclusive licensee of Jockey in India and nearby markets (and Speedo in India), making innerwear and athleisure in its own Karnataka factories and paying a royalty to Jockey International
strengths: Dominant premium innerwear brand that holds price through cycles
Own manufacturing and very wide outlet reach
risks: Q2 FY27 profit rose only 4% as input costs climbed; volumes grew about 5.5%
Royalty and licence renewal with Jockey International
Value innerwear (Zudio, quick commerce) and new D2C brands

ablbl.name: Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands
ablbl.role: Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly and Peter England menswear plus American Eagle and Reebok in India; demerged from ABFRL and listed Jun 2025
strengths: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 11% to ₹2,266 Cr and profit more than doubled; 3,434 stores (31 Oct 2026)
Like-for-like 5.3% despite Diwali moving to Q3
risks: Office-wear demand and discounting
Emerging brands (American Eagle, Reebok) still low-margin

abfrl.name: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail
abfrl.role: After the 2025 demerger: Pantaloons and Style Up stores, TCNS (W, Aurelia), Tasva and designer labels (Sabyasachi, Tarun Tahiliani, House of Masaba)
strengths: Pantaloons is a large value-fashion chain; ethnic and designer labels add wedding exposure
Pantaloons grew about 6% in Q2 FY27
risks: Revenue grew only 2% and it lost ₹376 Cr in Q2 FY27
Debt and losses in newer brands
Value chains (Zudio) compete with Pantaloons

arvindfasn.name: Arvind Fashions
arvindfasn.role: Licensee and owner of US Polo Assn, Arrow, Flying Machine and Tommy Hilfiger and Calvin Klein in India (through a JV with PVH)
strengths: US Polo Assn is one of India's largest casualwear brands
Shift from wholesale to own stores and online
risks: Royalties to licensors and renewal risk
Discount-heavy categories

raymondlsl.name: Raymond Lifestyle
raymondlsl.role: Raymond suiting fabric, The Raymond Shop stores and Park Avenue, ColorPlus and Parx brands, plus garment exports; demerged from Raymond in 2024
strengths: Leader in suiting fabric for weddings
Large franchise store network in small towns
risks: Wedding-season dependence
Fabric demand shifting to ready-made

gocolors.name: Go Fashion (India)
gocolors.role: Go Colors women's bottom-wear (leggings, palazzos, jeggings) through its own stores and large-format chains
strengths: Category creator in branded women's bottoms
risks: Narrow category; same-store growth has slowed

kprmill.name: K.P.R. Mill
kprmill.role: Tiruppur-region yarn, knitted fabric and garment exporter (also its FASO innerwear brand), with sugar and ethanol plants
strengths: Fibre-to-garment integration with one of India's largest garment capacities
Q2 FY27 profit rose about 58% to ₹345 Cr as margins widened
risks: Part of Q2 FY27 margin came from cheap cotton inventory, which won't repeat
Export customers concentrated in a few global brands
Sugar and ethanol add policy risk

vtl.name: Vardhman Textiles
vtl.role: One of India's largest cotton-yarn spinners, with fabric, sewing thread and acrylic fibre, based in Punjab
strengths: Q2 FY27 profit rose about 91% to ₹359 Cr as low-cost cotton was spun at higher yarn prices
Net cash and scale in yarn
risks: Yarn volumes flat; fabric weaker
Margins fall when cotton stocks are bought at current prices

arvind.name: Arvind
arvind.role: Lalbhai group maker of denim, shirting and knits, garments for global brands and advanced materials (technical textiles)
strengths: Large denim and woven fabric capacity with garmenting
Technical textiles diversify income
risks: US tariff and order swings
Cotton and dye costs

gokex.name: Gokaldas Exports
gokex.role: Bengaluru-based garment exporter for global brands, with plants in Kenya (Atraco) and India
strengths: One of India's largest apparel exporters
Kenya plants give duty-free access to the US under AGOA when in force
risks: Most sales go to US brands; tariffs set orders
Labour costs and productivity

bata.name: Bata India
bata.role: India's largest footwear retailer by stores (Bata, Hush Puppies, Power, North Star), selling through company and franchise stores
strengths: Fourth straight quarter of growth: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 7.5% to ₹862 Cr
Brand trust and franchise expansion in small towns
risks: EBITDA margin fell to 16.7% in Q2 FY27 as the festive season shifted
Losing younger buyers to sneaker and online brands
Royalty to the Bata group

metrobrand.name: Metro Brands
metrobrand.role: Premium footwear chain (Metro, Mochi, Walkway) that also runs Crocs, Fila and Foot Locker stores in India
strengths: Highest margins in Indian footwear retail
Foot Locker and Crocs add sneaker exposure
risks: Premium rentals in malls
Foot Locker rollout costs

relaxo.name: Relaxo Footwears
relaxo.role: Mass-market rubber and EVA slippers and sports shoes (Sparx, Flite, Bahamas) sold through distributors in small towns
strengths: Largest maker by pairs with in-house manufacturing
Low-price leadership
risks: Volumes have stagnated as mass buyers trade down or up
Rubber and EVA prices

campus.name: Campus Activewear
campus.role: Sports and athleisure shoe brand priced mostly under ₹3,000, sold through dealers, its own stores and online
strengths: Leader in affordable sports shoes in small cities
Benefits from BIS rules curbing cheap imports
risks: Competition from online brands and global sportswear
Distributor credit

redtape.name: Redtape
redtape.role: Sneakers, casual shoes and apparel sold largely online and through its own stores; demerged from Mirza International
strengths: Fast-growing value sneaker brand online
risks: Heavy reliance on marketplaces
Fashion risk in sneakers

titan.name: Titan Company
titan.role: Tata group's jewellery (Tanishq, Mia, Zoya, CaratLane), watches (Titan, Fastrack) and eyewear company, India's largest organised jeweller
strengths: Q2 FY27 income rose 25% to ₹20,533 Cr; jewellery about 21%, watches about 30%; 3,758 stores
Most-trusted jewellery brand gaining share from family jewellers
Gold-exchange and saving schemes lock in buyers
risks: Q2 FY27 profit includes ₹536 Cr of one-time customs-duty gains; adjusted PBT rose 18%
High gold prices cut grams bought (buyer growth mid-single digit)
International expansion costs

kalyan.name: Kalyan Jewellers India
kalyan.role: Kerala-born jewellery chain across India and the Gulf, expanding through franchise-owned showrooms, plus Candere online
strengths: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31% to ₹10,323 Cr; India profit up 62%; targets 25% FY27 growth
Franchise model expands showrooms with partners' capital
risks: Q2 FY27 profit includes a ₹73 Cr exceptional gain
Thinner margins than Titan; unhedged gold exposure
Middle East business is slower

thangamayil.name: Thangamayil Jewellery
thangamayil.role: Madurai-based gold jewellery chain with about 66 showrooms in Tamil Nadu's smaller towns, now entering Chennai
strengths: Same-store sales rose about 36% in H1 FY27 on gold prices and exchange
Regional trust in a gold-heavy state
risks: Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 40% but profit was flat as margins fell about 1.5 points
Plain-gold mix gives thin making charges
Single-state concentration

senco.name: Senco Gold
senco.role: Kolkata-based jewellery chain, the leader in East India, with own and franchise showrooms and lightweight Everlite and Gossip lines
strengths: Strong in East India and in lightweight jewellery for high gold prices
risks: Regional concentration
Gold-loan funding and hedging costs

pngjl.name: P N Gadgil Jewellers
pngjl.role: Pune-based jewellery chain across Maharashtra and Goa with a US store; listed Sep 2024
strengths: Strong regional brand with franchise-led growth
risks: Bullion-trading revenue inflates sales with little margin
Maharashtra concentration

bluestone.name: BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle
bluestone.role: Online-first diamond and gold jewellery brand with its own manufacturing and a growing store chain; listed Aug 2025
strengths: Design-led studded jewellery with higher making margins
risks: Loss-making while adding stores
Lab-grown diamonds and Titan's CaratLane compete

ethos.name: Ethos
ethos.role: India's largest luxury and premium watch retailer for Swiss brands, with a certified pre-owned business; promoted by KDDL
strengths: Dealer for most Swiss brands with prime mall stores
Pre-owned watches add a second revenue stream
risks: Brands can move to direct retail
High inventory per store

rajeshexpo.name: Rajesh Exports
rajeshexpo.role: Bengaluru gold refiner and jewellery manufacturer (owns Swiss refiner Valcambi) supplying gold and finished jewellery to retailers
strengths: Refining and jewellery manufacturing at large scale give jewellers a supply source
risks: SEBI interim order (3 Jun 2026) alleges overstated subsidiary revenue and fund diversion; the company denies it
Sells to the trade, so its link to jewellery chains is indirect
Gold price swings

trent.name: Trent
trent.role: Tata group's fashion retailer - Zudio (value), Westside (own-label department stores) and Star (grocery), plus a Zara JV with Inditex
strengths: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 22.5% to ₹5,788 Cr; Zudio opened its 1,000th store
Own labels and weekly drops keep prices low and margins high (operating EBIT margin 11.6% in Q2 FY27)
risks: Same-store growth has slowed as Zudio matures
Value rivals (Vishal, Reliance's Yousta) copy the format

vmm.name: Vishal Mega Mart
vmm.role: Value hypermarket chain for clothes, home goods and groceries in tier-2 to tier-4 towns, mostly under its own labels; listed 18 Dec 2024
strengths: 844 stores in 582 cities (30 Sep 2026); own brands about 72.5% of product sales
Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14% to ₹3,399 Cr
risks: Reported Q2 FY27 same-store growth slowed to 5.4% (about 9% adjusted for Diwali)
Profit grew only about 4% in Q2 FY27
DMart, Reliance and quick commerce compete in groceries

dmart.name: Avenue Supermarts (DMart)
dmart.role: Grocery-led hypermarket chain whose general merchandise and apparel aisles compete directly with value fashion and home-goods chains
strengths: Lowest-cost store model in Indian retail; owns most of its stores
risks: Apparel is a small share of its sales

vmart.name: V-Mart Retail
vmart.role: Value fashion chain in tier-2 and tier-3 towns of North and East India, plus Unlimited stores in the South
strengths: Deep small-town footprint in UP and Bihar
risks: Rural and small-town spending swings
Competition from Zudio and Vishal

shoppersstop.name: Shoppers Stop
shoppersstop.role: K Raheja Corp department-store chain selling third-party and own brands, plus Intune value fashion stores and beauty stores
strengths: Loyalty base among metro department-store shoppers
Intune targets the value segment
risks: Department-store footfalls shifting to value chains and online
Lease costs

relianceRetail.name: Reliance Retail
relianceRetail.role: India's largest retailer: Trends, Yousta and Azorte fashion, Reliance Digital electronics, Smart Bazaar grocery, Ajio and Tira
strengths: Largest store network across fashion, electronics and grocery
risks: Unlisted

lenskart.name: Lenskart Solutions
lenskart.role: Eyewear chain with about 2,700 stores in India that makes its own frames and lenses; also sells online
strengths: Own factory lifts margins above those of multi-brand optical shops
Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 43%
risks: Store growth needs steady capex
Rich valuation since its Nov 2025 listing
Online and store sales are reported together

jubilant.name: Jubilant FoodWorks
jubilant.role: Master franchisee of Domino's Pizza in India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh and owner of Domino's Turkey, plus Popeyes and Hong's Kitchen
strengths: Domino's India like-for-like up 4.1% and delivery up 11.3% in Q2 FY27; 2,601 Domino's stores
Own app keeps most delivery off aggregator commissions
risks: Royalty to Domino's Pizza Inc. and renewal terms
Cheese and wheat costs
Turkey's inflation weighs on group results (Eurasia LFL -2.1%)

devyani.name: Devyani International
devyani.role: Yum's largest franchisee in India - KFC, Pizza Hut and Costa Coffee - plus Biryani By Kilo and stores in Thailand and Nigeria; merging Sapphire Foods into itself
strengths: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 10.4% to ₹1,519 Cr; added 70 stores
CCI cleared the Sapphire merger (Nov 2026), creating one operator with nearly 3,000 stores
risks: Pizza Hut same-store sales still weak
Merger integration and Yum's revised franchise terms
Profit is thin at current same-store growth

sapphire.name: Sapphire Foods India
sapphire.role: Yum franchisee running KFC and Pizza Hut in South and West India and in Sri Lanka; to merge into Devyani (177 Devyani shares per 100)
strengths: Strong KFC network in the South and Sri Lanka
risks: Stock will be swapped into Devyani once the merger completes
Pizza Hut losses

westlife.name: Westlife Foodworld
westlife.role: McDonald's franchisee for West and South India, running restaurants, McCafé and drive-throughs
strengths: Same-store sales rose 10.1% in Q2 FY27, the best in 13 quarters, with double-digit guest growth; revenue up 16% to ₹747 Cr
risks: Profit thin after expansion and depreciation (small loss reported in Q2 FY27)
Royalty to McDonald's
Chicken and dairy costs

rba.name: Restaurant Brands Asia
rba.role: Burger King franchisee for India, with BK Café, plus a Burger King business in Indonesia
strengths: Value-led burger menu growing in small cities
risks: Still loss-making at the group level
Royalty and development commitments to Burger King

travelfood.name: Travel Food Services
travelfood.role: Runs quick-service restaurants and food courts at airports, including KFC and Subway franchises, besides its lounges
strengths: Long concessions at major Indian airports
risks: Concession fees take a large share of sales
Concentration in a few airport groups and their re-tenders
Airport footfall, not city demand, sets its sales

eternal.name: Eternal (Zomato, Blinkit)
eternal.role: Food-delivery platform (Zomato) through which restaurant chains reach customers for a commission; District sells cinema tickets
strengths: Largest food-delivery reach for QSR chains
risks: Commissions squeeze chains' delivery margins

swiggy.name: Swiggy
swiggy.role: No. 2 food-delivery app used by QSR chains, plus Dineout restaurant bookings
strengths: Second channel for chains' delivery orders
risks: Commission rates and discount funding

unitedspirits.name: United Spirits
unitedspirits.role: Diageo's Indian arm and the largest spirits maker - McDowell's, Royal Challenge, Signature, Black Dog, Smirnoff and imported Johnnie Walker
strengths: Prestige-and-above now about 94% of sales value; grew about 6% in Q2 FY27
Imported Scotch (Johnnie Walker) gains from the UK FTA duty cut
risks: Mass 'popular' brands fell about 23% in Q2 FY27 on Maharashtra and Karnataka policy
Standalone profit slipped about 2% in Q2 FY27 on higher advertising
State pricing approvals

ubl.name: United Breweries
ubl.role: India's largest brewer (Kingfisher, Heineken, Amstel), controlled by Heineken
strengths: Q2 FY27 volumes rose 16%, premium 38%; Heineken Silver up 67%, Kingfisher Ultra 44%
Profit nearly tripled to about ₹136 Cr on a weak base
risks: Beer is weather-sensitive and taxed differently by each state
Receivable delays from state corporations
Barley and glass costs

radico.name: Radico Khaitan
radico.role: Maker of Magic Moments vodka (India's largest), 8PM and premium whiskies (Rampur single malt, Royal Ranthambore, Jaisalmer gin), with its own grain distilleries
strengths: Prestige volumes rose 36% to a record 5.28 million cases in Q2 FY27; profit up 66%
Own malt and grain distilling gives cost control
risks: Packaging cost hit of about ₹27 Cr in Q2 FY27
Maharashtra excise changes
Grain prices linked to ethanol demand

abdl.name: Allied Blenders and Distillers
abdl.role: Maker of Officer's Choice whisky (mass), Sterling Reserve and ICONiQ White (premium); listed 2 Jul 2024
strengths: Record 10 million cases in Q2 FY27; revenue up 15.8%
ICONiQ White grew 20.6% to 3.2 million cases
risks: Officer's Choice Blue only just stopped declining
Mass whisky most exposed to state excise hikes

tilaknagar.name: Tilaknagar Industries
tilaknagar.role: Mansion House brandy maker that bought Pernod Ricard's Imperial Blue whisky (completed 1 Dec 2025), becoming a national IMFL player
strengths: Leads brandy in the South; Imperial Blue adds one of India's largest whisky brands
risks: Debt and integration after the ₹3,442 Cr Imperial Blue deal
Brandy concentrated in a few southern states

globusspr.name: Globus Spirits
globusspr.role: Grain-based extra-neutral alcohol maker in Rajasthan, Haryana, West Bengal and Bihar, with country liquor and its own IMFL brands
strengths: Supplies grain spirit to other brands and its own country liquor
risks: Grain prices; ethanol demand for fuel competes for supply
Small brand portfolio

sdbl.name: Som Distilleries & Breweries
sdbl.role: Madhya Pradesh-based beer (Hunter, Woodpecker, Black Fort) and spirits maker selling mainly in Central and South India
strengths: Fast-growing strong-beer brands in Karnataka and MP
risks: State policy concentration
Past regulatory issues

sula.name: Sula Vineyards
sula.role: India's largest winemaker (Nashik), with wine tourism; wine was spared Maharashtra's 2025 excise hike
strengths: Dominant share of Indian wine and own vineyards
risks: Wine is a small, slow-growing category
Imported wine may get cheaper under trade deals

pernodIndia.name: Pernod Ricard India
pernodIndia.role: No. 2 spirits company: Royal Stag, Blenders Pride, 100 Pipers, Chivas Regal and Jameson; sold Imperial Blue to Tilaknagar in 2025
strengths: Royal Stag and Blenders Pride lead in premium whisky
risks: Unlisted

pvrinox.name: PVR INOX
pvrinox.role: India's largest multiplex chain after the 2023 PVR-INOX merger, earning on tickets, food and beverages and screen ads
strengths: Q2 FY27 average ticket price and food spend per head each rose about 14%, footfalls about 4% (reported)
Asset-light screens with mall developers
risks: Depends on a steady film slate
Streaming windows and rents
Debt from the merger years

cinepolis.name: Cinépolis India
cinepolis.role: Mexican chain's Indian multiplex arm, India's No. 3 cinema operator
strengths: Premium formats and mall partnerships
risks: Unlisted

wonderla.name: Wonderla Holidays
wonderla.role: Amusement and water parks in Kochi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Bhubaneswar and Chennai, earning on entry tickets plus food and merchandise
strengths: Owns its parks; high food and merchandise spend per visitor
risks: Footfalls fall in heavy-rain quarters
New parks take years to fill

imagicaa.name: Imagicaaworld Entertainment
imagicaa.role: Imagica theme, water and snow parks at Khopoli near Mumbai plus Wet'n Joy parks in Lonavala and Shirdi
strengths: Largest theme park near Mumbai and Pune
risks: Seasonal footfalls
Expansion funding

phoenix.name: The Phoenix Mills
phoenix.role: Mall owner (Palladium, Phoenix Marketcity) whose tenants include PVR INOX screens, food courts and the store chains here
strengths: Retailer sales in its malls are a read on premium spending
risks: Earns rent, not retail margin

nexusReit.name: Nexus Select Trust
nexusReit.role: India's only listed retail REIT: owns 17 malls that host multiplexes, food courts and fashion stores
strengths: Revenue-share leases let rent grow with tenant sales
Grade A malls in many cities
risks: Rent, not ticket sales, is its income, so the link to cinemas is indirect
Discretionary slowdown and online competition

igi.name: International Gemological Institute
igi.role: Grades and certifies lab-grown and natural diamonds and jewellery for jewellers and retailers; Blackstone-controlled, listed Dec 2024
strengths: Market leader in lab-grown diamond certification
High margins with little capital needed
risks: Lab-grown diamond prices keep falling
Competition from GIA and other labs

skyGold.name: Sky Gold and Diamonds
skyGold.role: B2B jewellery maker supplying lightweight gold jewellery to chains such as Malabar, Kalyan and Joyalukkas
strengths: Grows with the big jewellery chains' store expansion
Own manufacturing in Navi Mumbai
risks: A few large customers buy most of its output
Gold prices drive working capital

vedantFashions.name: Vedant Fashions
vedantFashions.role: Owns Manyavar, Mohey and Twamev, India's largest ethnic and wedding-wear brand, sold through franchised stores
strengths: Dominant brand in men's wedding wear
Asset-light franchise model with high margins
risks: Sales have slowed with softer wedding demand
Women's wear (Mohey) is still small

kewalKiran.name: Kewal Kiran Clothing
kewalKiran.role: Owns the Killer jeans, Integriti, Easies and Lawman menswear brands, sold through own stores and multi-brand outlets
strengths: Debt-free with its own manufacturing
Long-running youth denim brand
risks: Small beside the large apparel retailers
Fashion and inventory risk

dollar.name: Dollar Industries
dollar.role: Innerwear and athleisure maker (Dollar Bigboss, Missy, Force NXT) selling through dealers and modern trade
strengths: Strong value-innerwear brand in North and East India
Integrated knitting and processing
risks: Cotton yarn price swings
Crowded mass innerwear market

luxInd.name: Lux Industries
luxInd.role: Kolkata innerwear maker (Lux Cozi, ONN, GenX) selling mostly through dealers
strengths: One of India's largest innerwear brands by volume
Wide dealer network
risks: Margins squeezed by yarn costs and competition
Mass segment with little pricing power

rupa.name: Rupa & Company
rupa.role: Kolkata innerwear maker (Rupa Frontline, Euro, Macroman) selling through dealers and modern trade
strengths: Long-established innerwear brands
Low debt
risks: Slow growth in its core mass segment
Yarn price swings

indoCount.name: Indo Count Industries
indoCount.role: One of the world's largest bed-linen makers, supplying US retailers and building its own brands in the US
strengths: Scale and long ties with big US retailers
US brands and a US plant to sell closer to customers
risks: US tariffs on Indian textiles
Cotton price swings

himatsingka.name: Himatsingka Seide
himatsingka.role: Bed-linen, towel and drapery maker exporting to US retailers, under its own and licensed brands
strengths: Integrated from yarn to finished bedding
Brand licences sold through US retailers
risks: High debt
US tariffs and retailer destocking

cello.name: Cello World
cello.role: Houseware and moulded furniture maker (Cello) selling bottles, kitchenware, glassware and plastic furniture to homes
strengths: Strong houseware brand with wide distribution
Own glassware plant reduces reliance on imports
risks: Competition from Milton and unbranded makers
Plastic raw-material costs

barbeque.name: United Foodbrands (Barbeque Nation)
barbeque.role: Runs Barbeque Nation buffet restaurants in India and abroad, plus Toscano and Salt
strengths: Well-known casual-dining brand
Expanding into smaller cities
risks: Has made losses as same-store sales fell
Competition from cheaper dining and delivery

electronicsMart.name: Electronics Mart India
electronicsMart.role: Runs Bajaj Electronics, a consumer-electronics and appliance chain in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, now expanding into NCR
strengths: Strong regional brand and store economics
Grows with appliance and phone demand
risks: Thin retail margins
Competition from online, Croma and Reliance Digital

v2Retail.name: V2 Retail
v2Retail.role: Value-fashion chain in tier-2 and tier-3 towns of North and East India
strengths: Fast store expansion
Low price points that suit small-town shoppers
risks: Competition from V-Mart, Zudio and Reliance Trends
Inventory and store rents

rrKabel.name: RR Kabel
rrKabel.role: Wire and cable maker whose consumer arm sells fans, lights, switches and appliances (Luminous fans and lights, bought in 2022)
strengths: Shares distribution with its large house-wire business
Luminous brand recognition
risks: Consumer electricals have made losses
Fan and lighting competition from Crompton, Havells and Orient

stoveKraft.name: Stove Kraft
stoveKraft.role: Kitchen-appliance and cookware maker selling Pigeon and Gilma, and Black+Decker home appliances under licence
strengths: Pigeon is a strong value brand, especially in South India
Own manufacturing keeps costs low
risks: Low-price segment with thin margins
Competition from TTK Prestige and Hawkins

suryaRoshni.name: Surya Roshni
suryaRoshni.role: Steel pipe maker whose consumer arm sells LED lighting, fans and appliances
strengths: Large lighting brand in small towns and rural India
Steel pipes give it scale
risks: Consumer products are the smaller part of its sales
LED price deflation

epack.name: EPACK Durable
epack.role: Contract maker of room ACs, AC components and small appliances for consumer brands
strengths: One of India's largest contract makers of room ACs
Adding new brand customers and component plants
risks: Sales tied to the AC season and a few brand customers
Thin margins typical of contract manufacturing

siyaram.name: Siyaram Silk Mills
siyaram.role: Makes suiting and shirting fabrics (Siyaram's, Mistair) and readymade garments (Oxemberg, J Hampstead)
strengths: Strong fabric brand in small towns
Growing garment exports
risks: Shift from tailored to readymade clothing
Depends on wedding and festive seasons

pearlGlobal.name: Pearl Global Industries
pearlGlobal.role: Garment exporter making apparel for US and European brands from plants in India, Bangladesh, Vietnam and Indonesia
strengths: Plants in several countries let buyers spread tariff and supply risk
Long ties with large US brands
risks: US tariff changes
Depends on a few large brand customers

piccadily.name: Piccadily Agro Industries
piccadily.role: Makes Indri single-malt whisky and other premium spirits, alongside a sugar mill
strengths: Indri has won global awards and sells in many countries
Own distillery and maturing stock
risks: Malt whisky ties up years of stock and cash
State excise and pricing rules

apple.name: Apple (India operations)
apple.role: The largest brand making phones in India - iPhones are assembled by Foxconn and Tata Electronics, mostly for export
strengths: iPhone exports reached about ₹2L Cr in FY26, India's single largest branded export (Business Today, Apr 2026)
Roughly one in four iPhones sold worldwide in 2025 was assembled in India
risks: Not listed in India; exposure only through its assemblers and suppliers
US trade policy and tariffs decide how much export volume stays in India
notes: Apple Inc. is listed in the US (NASDAQ: AAPL); its Indian subsidiaries are not listed
Its contract manufacturers, not Apple itself, would claim MPMS incentives

samsung.name: Samsung India Electronics
samsung.role: Runs one of the world's largest phone factories at Noida, making Galaxy phones for India and export
strengths: Plans to make Galaxy S26 flagships in Noida (Mar 2026)
Large enough to qualify for MPMS Track 1 on its own
risks: Not listed in India
Its earlier PLI benefits ended in FY25; future incentives depend on clearing MPMS growth hurdles
notes: Subsidiary of Samsung Electronics (Korea Exchange); not listed in India
Also outsources some models to Indian EMS firms such as Dixon

lava.name: Lava International
lava.role: India's main home-grown phone brand, the most likely candidate for MPMS Track 2 (Indian brands)
strengths: Indian-owned with in-house design - the profile Track 2 rewards with 5% plus 3% for design and R&D
CLSA named it the domestic brand most likely to benefit (Aug 2026)
risks: Small share of a market dominated by Chinese-linked brands, Samsung and Apple
IPO plans have been delayed repeatedly
notes: Unlisted; filed draft IPO papers in 2021, listing pushed to FY27 or later per reports
Track 2 needs ₹1,000 Cr FY26 turnover and passing a five-part Indian-brand test

redington.name: Redington
redington.role: Large IT and mobility distributor - distributes iPhones and other smartphones across India
strengths: Scale distributor with long-standing Apple relationship, so it benefits from rising India iPhone sales
Low valuation and dividend yield versus EMS stocks
risks: Distribution margins are thin (around 1-2% net)
Benefits from phone demand, not from MPMS incentives directly

moschip.name: MosChip Technologies
moschip.role: Hyderabad chip-design services company (ASIC, SoC, embedded) building its own product designs
strengths: One of very few listed Indian pure plays on chip design
Revenue rose from ₹148 Cr (FY22) to ₹585 Cr (FY26)
risks: Mostly services revenue; product bets are early
High valuation for a services business

lt.name: Larsen & Toubro
lt.role: L&T's wholly owned fabless chip unit (LTSCT): power, analog and silicon-carbide chips for autos, industry and energy
strengths: Showed 40 products including its first 1,200V silicon-carbide MOSFET at SEMICON India (Sep 2026)
Agreed with Tata Electronics (18 Sep 2026) to explore making and packaging its chips in India
L&T invested ₹542 Cr in the unit in FY26 (₹859 Cr cumulative)
risks: Tiny relative to L&T's ₹2.86L Cr revenue - no visible impact on the stock yet
Revenue target of US$500m by FY31 is ambitious and unproven

cyient.name: Cyient
cyient.role: Engineering services company that set up Cyient Semiconductors (Apr 2025) for custom chips (ASICs) and its own fabless products
strengths: 25+ years of ASIC work for industrial, data-centre, auto and medical clients
Aims to build India's first fabless chip product company (Investor Day, Aug 2026)
risks: Semiconductor unit is small inside a much larger engineering-services business
No disclosed product revenue milestones yet

tataProjects.name: Tata Projects
tataProjects.role: EPC contractor that built Micron's Sanand ATMP plant
strengths: Delivered India's first large chip-packaging plant for Micron (contract Sep 2023), a rare cleanroom track record in India
risks: Unlisted; no public market data
Construction margins are thin and project-dependent
notes: Tata Electronics separately signed Taiwan's Kelington for Dholera fab infrastructure (Sep 2026)

ionExchange.name: Ion Exchange (India)
ionExchange.role: Water-treatment company that makes ultra-pure water (UPW) and zero-discharge systems
strengths: Already supplies UPW systems for solar cell plants (₹205 Cr orders, Dec 2025) - the same technology fabs need
Recurring resin, chemical and service income after each installation
risks: No disclosed semiconductor UPW order yet
FY26 profit fell to ₹143 Cr on project-margin pressure

blueStar.name: Blue Star
strengths: Large project business that builds controlled-environment HVAC for factories and data centres
Strong balance sheet and execution record
risks: Semiconductor cleanrooms are a small niche in a consumer-AC-heavy business
Foreign cleanroom specialists compete for fab packages

thermax.name: Thermax
thermax.role: Utility systems: boilers, chillers, water treatment and captive power for industrial campuses
strengths: Supplies the heating, cooling and water utilities large plants need
Broad industrial customer base
risks: Chip-plant orders are not separately disclosed
Utility packages for fabs often go to specialist foreign vendors

dixon.name: Dixon Technologies
dixon.role: India's largest home-grown EMS company and biggest Indian phone assembler (Samsung, Motorola, Xiaomi, Vivo and others)
strengths: Brokerages (Macquarie, JPMorgan) call it the clearest MPMS beneficiary
Vivo JV approved (Jul 2026) adds a large anchor customer; ~₹1,100 Cr of phone exports in Q1 FY27
Building camera and display module plants that can earn part of the 1.5% sourcing bonus
risks: CLSA cut it to Underperform (Aug 2026): much of its sales may miss the hurdle unless exports grow
Kotak estimates MPMS adds only 0.14-0.22 percentage points to EBITDA margin
Thin margins and high customer concentration

foxconn.name: Foxconn India (incl. Bharat FIH)
foxconn.role: Foxconn group's Indian plants: its Tamil Nadu unit assembles most of India's iPhones, and Bharat FIH builds phones for other brands
strengths: The core iPhone export assembler; Bharat FIH is described as India's largest EMS provider
Bharat FIH has SEBI approval for a ~₹5,000 Cr IPO
risks: Not yet listed in India
Heavily dependent on Apple volumes and US trade policy
